commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Warn only on per-request do_normalize/do_rescale overrides
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `mm_device_do_normalize` on, the default for the Qwen2/2.5/3-VL family, every process that builds the HF processor warns that it is ignoring per-request `do_normalize` and `do_rescale`, with no request involved. This warns only when a request actually asks for normalization.

## Claims

- No warning at startup: building dummy image inputs makes 0 `warning_once` calls instead of 10.
- A request that sets `do_normalize` or `do_rescale` still gets the warning; before, the startup calls had already spent the `warning_once`, so it never appeared.
- The merged kwargs are unchanged, so outputs are not affected.

## Validation

On main (`6ad2e06c4a`) with and without this commit, on CPU with the Qwen3-VL processor: count `warning_once` calls while building dummy image inputs, then merge request kwargs.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| warnings while building dummy image inputs | 10 | 0 |
| request `do_normalize=False` | 1 | 0 |
| request `do_normalize=True, do_rescale=True` | 2 | 2 |
| merged kwargs | `do_normalize=False, do_rescale=False` | same |

```text
pytest -q tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py
83 passed
```

## Details

`InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` merges the kwargs through `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs`, which forces both keys to `False`, and `cached_processor_from_config` then merges the result again. The second merge sees the forced `False` values as request kwargs and warns. The warning came with #56798. Warning only on a truthy request value fixes that without touching either merge: a request that passes `False` is not overridden, so there is nothing to report.

No open PR addresses this. The open PRs that mention `mm_device_do_normalize` (#58972, #57924) extend it to other models and do not touch this warning.

commits.pr_title: [Build] Migrate vendored DeepGEMM from pybind to TORCH_LIBRARY (abi3)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM. Here, we are not migrating deep_gemm to the stable abi yet, but are moving it off of pybind and onto TORCH_LIBRARY. Once we make these updates, we will open a seperate PR to make deep_gemm torch ABI stable. This points to the DeepGEMM updates in the PR https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/393

- Pin DeepGEMM to `cleonard530/DeepGEMM` (`migrate_pybind_to_torch_library`) so vLLM vendors the TORCH_LIBRARY + abi3 layout instead of pybind11. If this works, we will need to discuss how we want to merge`cleonard530/DeepGEMM`. vLLM has a fork of `DeepGEMM`, but currently the build still points towards upstream.   
- Replace the per-Python `g++` build of `_C.cpython-*.so` with a single `_C_extension.abi3.so` built via DeepGEMM’s `setup.py`, plus `deep_gemm/_C.py` as the `torch.ops.deep_gemm` shim.
- Update cmake / wheel checks / install script for the new artifacts (`_C.py` + `_C_extension*.so`) and drop `DEEPGEMM_PYTHON_INTERPRETERS` / `TARGET_PY`.
This closes the per-interpreter DeepGEMM binding path tracked after the failed single-abi3 attempt (#41476 / #41512) and implements the TORCH_LIBRARY direction noted in #42431.

@janeyx99 @Harry-Chen 

## Test Plan
```
  python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py
```

## Test Result

- tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py - `PASS`
- tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py - `100 failed, 322 passed`, all failures are `fatal error: sanitizer/asan_interface.h: No such file or directory`. Not related to TORCH_LIBRARY migration
- tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py - `PASS`
- tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py - `PASS`
- tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py - `PASS`

commits.pr_title: [CI][Rust Frontend] Pass `--locked` to cargo binstall
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Pass `--locked` to the three `cargo binstall` calls in `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (cargo-sort, cargo-deny, cargo-nextest), so that binstall's source-build fallback uses each tool's shipped `Cargo.lock`.

## Claims

- Fixes `Rust Frontend Cargo` failing before any test runs whenever binstall falls back to building cargo-nextest from source.
- Makes the cargo-sort and cargo-deny fallbacks reproducible, as cargo-deny's README recommends (`cargo install --locked cargo-deny`).
- No change on the normal path: binstall only forwards `--locked` to the `cargo install` fallback, and the prebuilt download is unaffected.

## Validation

With the CI version of cargo-binstall (1.20.1), forcing the source fallback via `--strategies compile` into a scratch `--root`:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo binstall --no-confirm --force --secure --strategies compile cargo-nextest@0.9` (current) | exit 70: `could not compile locked-tripwire` (resolves `0.1.1002`), same as CI |
| same + `--locked` | exit 0, cargo-nextest 0.9.146 (resolves `locked-tripwire 0.1.0` from the lockfile) |
| `cargo binstall --no-confirm --force --locked --strategies compile cargo-sort@2` | exit 0, cargo-sort 2.1.4 |
| `cargo binstall --no-confirm --force --locked --strategies compile cargo-deny@0.20` | exit 0, cargo-deny 0.20.2 |
| `cargo binstall --no-confirm --force --secure --locked cargo-nextest@0.9` (prebuilt path) | downloads the release binary in ~2 s |

`pre-commit` (incl. shellcheck) passes on the changed file.

## Details

In [Buildkite #93024](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93024) (vllm-project/vllm#59744), `:amd: (MI250) Rust Frontend Cargo` failed three times in a row with exit 70. binstall's unauthenticated GitHub API lookup for the nextest release returned `403 Forbidden`, so it timed out and fell back to `cargo install cargo-nextest` without `--locked`. That resolves every dependency to its newest semver-compatible version, including `locked-tripwire 0.1.1002`, which nextest publishes with a `compile_error!` (behind its `nextest` feature) to reject unlocked source installs; nextest's `Cargo.lock` pins `0.1.0`, which is empty. The CPU Cargo job passed on the same commit, and a fourth attempt an hour later passed.

This does not avoid the 403 itself, so a rate-limited agent still pays for a source build (about 80 s for cargo-nextest here) instead of the download. Giving binstall a GitHub token would avoid the fallback, but that touches agent secrets and is left out of this PR.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches the binstall calls in this script.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Clarify that vLLM does not isolate tenants sharing a server
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The security guide doesn't say whether vLLM isolates tenants that share a server, and the multimodal `uuid` section describes omitting `uuid` as safe. This adds a short Multi-Tenant Deployments section and fixes that recommendation to match.

## Claims

- New "Multi-Tenant Deployments" section in `docs/usage/security.md`: vLLM does not isolate tenants that share a server process, `cache_salt` is not an isolation boundary, and isolation should be handled in the deployment (an instance per tenant, or a gateway that scopes cache identifiers per tenant).
- The "Default behavior" bullet under Multimodal Media UUID Security no longer says omitting `uuid` is safe. It now says content-hash identity avoids accidental collisions but doesn't isolate tenants, and links to the new section.

## Validation

`pre-commit run --files docs/usage/security.md` passes (markdownlint-cli2, typos and the other applicable hooks). Docs-only change, no code or model behaviour affected.

## Details

This follows a discussion with the vLLM security team, who confirmed that isolation between tenants in one server process is outside vLLM's security scope and that `security.md` should say so.

Not a duplicate: #55478 adds a `uuid` warning to `docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md` but doesn't touch `security.md` or the default-behaviour recommendation. No other open PR changes these sections.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Eliminate staging from NCCL symmetric reduce-scatter
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Remove both staging copies from the modular MoE symmetric reduce-scatter path, building on #46703:

```text
Before: expert output → copy to registered input → ReduceScatter → copy to final output
After:  expert kernel / top-k reduction → registered input → ReduceScatter → final output
```

The optimization requires `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1`, uniform token counts, and NCCL >= 2.29.2. Unsupported configurations retain their existing fallbacks.

## Implementation

- Write expert output or contiguous top-k reduction directly into the registered combine buffer, and let NCCL write into the caller-owned final output.
- Reuse geometrically grown buffers, retaining old allocations for CUDA-graph replay and separating DBO microbatches.
- Preserve deterministic collectives, uneven-routing fallbacks, and CPU/ROCm behavior.

NCCL supports registered-send/nonregistered-receive ReduceScatter in [`ncclSymkPickKernel`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/blob/v2.29.2-1/src/sym_kernels.cc#L397-L416).

## Performance

Measured on 4×GB200 with NCCL 2.30.7. Operator latency and end-to-end throughput measure different effects; their percentage improvements are not additive.

### Reduce-scatter latency

BF16, hidden size 8192; latency in microseconds, lower is better. Latency reduction is `(staged − PR) / staged`.

| Output/rank | Staged symmetric | Direct symmetric (PR) | Latency reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.5 MiB | 42.4 | 35.6 | 16.0% |
| 1 MiB | 43.1 | 37.1 | 13.9% |
| 2 MiB | 42.3 | 37.4 | 11.6% |
| 4 MiB | 51.6 | 43.5 | 15.7% |
| 8 MiB | 84.8 | 76.7 | 9.6% |

Removing staging reduces symmetric reduce-scatter latency by **about 10–16%** over this range. Ordinary NCCL remains faster at some sizes.

### Nemotron Ultra end-to-end

Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4, TP1/DP4/EP4, default AG/RS backend, symmetric memory enabled in both baseline and PR. All changes below use the same convention: **PR / baseline − 1**, computed from geometric means. Higher throughput and lower TPOT/TTFT are better; concurrency is global.

| Workload (input / output tokens) | Concurrency | Output throughput | Mean TPOT | Mean TTFT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Long-prefill: 50,000 / 2,048 | 16 | +8.91% | −9.38% | −0.36% |
| Short-context: ~1,024 / 512 | 32 | +1.35% | −1.35% | −0.98% |
| Short-context: ~1,024 / 512 | 128 | +2.04% | −1.05% | −6.46% |
| Short-context: ~1,024 / 512 | 512 | +1.71% | −4.16% | +3.42% |

The long-prefill workload benefits most; its TTFT change is inconclusive. At short-context concurrency 32, throughput and TPOT improve in all six paired runs. Higher-concurrency results are mixed: **TTFT worsens in all six runs at concurrency 512**. These are two distinct workloads, not one concurrency-scaling curve.

E2E results compare baseline `5414b4e` with PR revision `622c1cc`; the current rebased head has not been benchmarked. The short-context sweep uses common instrumentation and disables Mamba stochastic rounding in both arms, so it is not a native-default deployment claim. No Super or multi-node scaling claim is made.

## Validation

- Local pre-commit checks, mypy, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Validated revision `3fbfae6`: **13 checks pass on 4×GB200, with no skips** (10 repository tests and 3 supplemental checks). Coverage includes caller-owned outputs, uneven routing, CPU/mocked-AITER regressions, buffer growth, and BF16/FP32 CUDA-graph replay after allocator churn.
- No separate model-accuracy suite was run; the E2E performance results above remain from the earlier revision.

AI tooling assisted inspection, testing, and analysis; the author remains responsible for the change.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Run pr-checklist before opening a PR
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make agents run the `pr-checklist` skill before they open a PR, drafts included. Right now they often skip it or put it off until the PR is marked ready. Follow-up to #57084 and #59638.

## Claims

- `pr-checklist` skill description: says when to use the skill (before opening a PR, drafts included, or before pushing review fixes). This is the text Claude Code reads when it decides whether to invoke a skill.
- `AGENTS.md`: replaces the advisory "Use ... before submitting a PR" with a concrete step that covers draft PRs. The line count is unchanged (159 lines).

## Validation

A/B test with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) in headless mode. Each run had its own clone and was given the same prompt: "the fix on this branch is committed; push it and open a draft PR to vllm-project/vllm". The test branch was a real bugfix (#60071) cherry-picked onto its parent commit, with `gh` replaced by a stub that only logs calls. Each run used one of two docs variants, with the variant folded into the base commit:

| Docs variant | Runs | Used pr-checklist before `gh pr create` (or before stopping) |
| ------------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `main` | 3 | 1/3 |
| this PR | 3 | 3/3 (2 via the Skill tool, 1 by reading `SKILL.md`) |

In the two `main` runs that skipped the checklist, the agent still did the other pre-PR steps listed in `AGENTS.md`: the duplicate-PR search, pre-commit, and tests. In one run of this PR's variant (new-1), the agent ran the checklist but then stopped without opening the PR, because it noticed the remote was not GitHub.

```bash
pre-commit run --files AGENTS.md .agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md  # passed
```

## Details

- Motivation: in practice, agents read "before submitting a PR" as "before marking ready for review". They open a draft and defer the checklist, as in #60210. The skill description also gave no trigger moment, so nothing linked the skill to `gh pr create`.
- Limitations: the sample is small (n=3 per variant) and used a single model and a single prompt. The runs also loaded the submitter's user-level Claude Code config. Wording alone cannot guarantee the checklist runs; a hard gate would need tooling such as a hook, which is out of scope here.
- Not a duplicate: #60111 edits section 4.3 of the same `SKILL.md` but not its frontmatter, so the two PRs do not conflict. No other open PR or issue covers this.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: pad gfx11 weight and activation strides
commits.pr_body:
On gfx11 (RDNA3/3.5) a W4A16 GEMM loses a large share of its achievable read bandwidth when an operand's row stride lands on a multiple of 1024 bytes. The rows alias into the same L2/DDR channels and the accesses serialize. Offsetting the stride by one 128 B cache line dodges it.

This PR nudges **both** operands off that cliff: the packed weight row (padded once at load) and the activation row (padded per call) and improves TTFT by up to 23 % and TPOT by up to 3 %.
Padding the activation (at runtime) pays for itself due to reduced GEMM time.

## The two cliffs

For weights, we pad at load time when they are a multiple of 1024 bytes. For activations,
we only pad when they are a multiple of 2048 bytes to ensure that their cost is recovered by the GEMM wins.

The following table shows how many GEMM shapes are affected by the padding in a model:

| Model | weight padded | 
|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` | 4/4 (`K=4096` → 2048 B, `K=12288` → 6144 B) | 
| `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-w4a16` | 4/4 (`K=14336` → 7168 B qualifies) | 
| `gemma-3-4b-it-quantized.w4a16` | 2/3 (`K=2048`, `K=10240`) |
| `Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` | 1/4 (`o_proj`, `K=4096`) |

Gated on gfx1151, where the effect was measured. This might also apply to other gfx11 parts, but we will need to measure and can enable as a follow up.

## Implementation

- `pack_skinny_int4` is the single source of truth for the skinny weight layout and applies the weight pad once at load.
- Activations are padded by an explicit copy inside the W4A16 apply op. The copy costs less than the GEMM gains by the strides. Having the activation's producer emit a padded output would make it free; that is a reasonable follow-up.
- **Activations are not padded on the decode path.** . This is why the decode win is preserved intact (see TPOT below).

## Benchmark

AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151), `--output-len 128 --num-prompts 10 --max-num-seqs 1 --request-rate 0.3`, median TTFT / TPOT, n as noted. Arms differ only in the files of this PR, on the same base commit and the same build.

| Model (in/out len) | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` 128/128 | 119.99 → 101.80 ms (**−15.2 %**) | 23.91 → 23.20 ms (**−3.0 %**) | 3/6 |
| `Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` 1920/128 | 1294.82 → 1191.71 ms (**−8.0 %**) | 25.95 → 25.29 ms (**−2.5 %**) | 3/3 |
| `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-w4a16` 128/128 | 131.50 → 101.75 ms (**−22.6 %**) | 22.37 → 21.86 ms (**−2.3 %**) | 3/6 |
| `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-w4a16` 1920/128 | 1243.30 → 1162.53 ms (**−6.5 %**) | 24.27 → 23.80 ms (**−1.9 %**) | 3/3 |
| `gemma-3-4b-it-quantized.w4a16` 1920/128 | 698.16 → 657.08 ms (**−5.9 %**) | 29.59 → 29.60 ms (no effect) | 3/3 |
| `Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` 1920/128 | 707.70 → 701.99 ms (**−0.8 %**) | 15.45 → 15.46 ms (no effect) | 3/3 |
| gemma-4-31B 328/256 | TTFT | 2408.500 [2405.490, 2409.240] | 2387.040 [2373.710, 2392.150] | 0.89 % |
| gemma-4-31B 328/256 | TPOT | 112.060 [111.960, 112.130] | 108.890 [108.700, 109.050] | **2.83 %** |
| gemma-4-31B 328/256 +MTP | TTFT | 2580.090 [2578.570, 2580.830] | 2545.780 [2542.360, 2549.050] | 1.33 % |
| gemma-4-31B 328/256 +MTP | TPOT | 55.790 [55.710, 55.960] | 51.450 [51.450, 51.490] | **7.78 %** |

Llama-3.1-8B is `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-w4a16-llmcompressor` (compressed-tensors, g128, symmetric).

`gemma-4-31B` is `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` (compressed-tensors
pack-quantized, 4-bit, group_size 32, asymmetric), 328 input / 256 output tokens
with one 640x480 image per request, `--mm-encoder-attn-backend TRITON_ATTN`.
`+MTP` adds `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",
"model":"google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`.

## Accuracy

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy (temperature 0.0), `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` on gfx1151, n=3 per arm:

| | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid | Output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR off | 88.00 % (3/3 reps identical) | 176 / 200 | 0.0 | 23209 (3/3) |
| this PR on | 88.00 % (3/3 reps identical) | 176 / 200 | 0.0 | 23209 – 23214 |

Identical accuracy on every rep of both arms. 

`tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` asserts that a row-padded weight produces bit-identical output to a dense one (`rtol=0, atol=0`) through both the HIP decode kernel and the Triton prefill kernel. **95 tests pass** on gfx1151 (`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`). Off gfx1151 the new code paths reduce to exactly the previous behaviour. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` is clean.

## Relation to other open PRs

This is the packed-int4 counterpart to #55090, which pads *dense* fp16/bf16 weight rows in `layers/linear.py`. Different tensors and code path, same underlying aliasing.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this PR. Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, and all tests, benchmarks and evals listed above were run on the hardware named.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Flag multi-branch allOf as unsupported for xgrammar

## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56556

Currently xgrammar do not support multi-branch allOf. The bug was already reported to xgrammar team, so we can use it as a tracker https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/937. Once the bug will be resolved on xgrammar side then we can enable it in vLLM. But for now we should properly process such requests and do not pass them to xgrammar.

This PR was made based on PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56557 done by [@ShaanveerS](https://github.com/shashankvarma499) (in respect to attempt put as a co-author to this PR).

In `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar.py` there were implemented a number of unit tests to cover multi-branch allOf. All the tests passed locally on my machine. To verify results run:

commits.pr_title: [vllm-bench, feature] Added support for Mooncake-style, timed-traces replay.
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Port `vllm bench serve`'s timed-trace replay to the Rust `vllm-bench` client: the `timed_trace` dataset (Mooncake-style JSONL: `{timestamp, input_length, output_length, hash_ids}`) and `--self-timed` scheduling, so recorded request-arrival schedules can be replayed faithfully from Rust. These 8 flags were previously allowlisted as `PYTHON_ONLY` in `rust/src/bench/tests/cli_parity.rs`; per that file's contract, this PR removes them.

## Example

```bash
vllm-bench \
  --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model glm-5.2-fp8 --tokenizer <tokenizer path> \
  --dataset-name timed_trace \
  --dataset-path trace.jsonl \
  --self-timed \
  --timed-trace-chunk-hash-size 16 \
  --timed-trace-sec-multiplier 0.001 \
  --num-prompts 1422
```

## Scope

Replays the shape of the traffic, not its content: arrival schedule, ISL/OSL, and prefix-sharing structure are preserved; prompt tokens are synthetic. Completions endpoint only. Complementary to #51104, which covers multi-turn HF datasets and intentionally excludes trace replay.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `timed_trace`, `self-timed`, and Rust bench trace replay: no open PR implements this.

## Test Plan

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p vllm-bench`
- Local schedule-fidelity check against a mock SSE server: 3-request trace with recorded offsets 0/2/4 s, with and without `--self-timed`.
- Live A/B against the Python client: same deployment, same 1,422-request agentic SWE trace (3,862 s recorded span), same nodes; only the benchmark client differs.

## Test Result

- `cargo test -p vllm-bench`: 170 passed, 0 failed (12 ignored: network). fmt and clippy clean.
- Mock-server fidelity: arrivals at 0 / 2.002 / 4.004 s with `--self-timed`; single burst with `--no-self-timed` (negative control).
- Live A/B:

| check | trace | Rust vllm-bench | Python `vllm bench serve` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| completed requests | 1,422 | 1,422 / 0 failed | 1,422 / 0 failed |
| served input tokens | 34,792,874 | exact | exact |
| served output tokens | 561,153 | exact | exact |
| duration vs recorded span | 3,862.29 s | +9.42 s (+0.244%)** | +9.51 s (+0.25%)** |
| server prefix-cache hit rate | 94.1% predicted | 93.9% | 93.9% |
| TTFT p50 / TPOT p50 | — | 172.0 ms / 15.96 ms | 175.5 ms / 15.99 ms |
| peak concurrency | — | 15 | 15 |

**The duration residual is the final request's service time after its on-schedule launch.

AI assistance was used to implement the change and run the tests. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and performed the live A/B evaluation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Honor speculative cacheability in SimpleCPU
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix lost CPU prefix-cache reuse during speculative decoding with eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Share the GPU coordinator's per-group cacheability rule with CPU store selection, and pass the configured prefill lookahead to the CPU coordinator.

Related: #54736, which is already merged and provides the underlying per-group offload geometry.

## Claims

- Prevent the CPU store cursor from permanently skipping blocks whose trailing KV is still re-prefillable during multi-module MTP.
- Preserve the extra cached draft block required by hybrid speculative prefix lookup.
- Preserve existing GPU cache-publication behavior by extracting its eligibility calculation into a shared helper.

## Validation

[Complete public reproducer, exact model config, patches, commands, and structured before/after records](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217).

Both GPU A/B cases use native `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` with a reduced config and **dummy weights**, three MTP modules, BF16, TP2/DCP2, model runner V2, a 64-token prefill budget, and real GPU/CPU transfers. The before/after columns compare separate unpatched and patched engines. Full reuse means matching that prompt's GPU-reusable prefix; block alignment and speculative cache-safety rules leave a suffix to recompute.

### Serial: the missing block persists across two CPU replays

Run one prompt at a time (`max_num_seqs=1`). For each prompt, clear both caches initially, then run **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 1 → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay 2 → GPU-hot control**. CPU caching survives both intermediate resets.

| Prompt tokens | CPU replay | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU before | CPU after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 1 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,257 | 2 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 1 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |
| 8,321 | 2 | 8,192 | **8,064** | **8,192** |

Both CPU replays have **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. The unpatched 8,321-token case stays one effective 128-token block short on the second CPU replay; the later 8,192-token GPU-hot hit is a separate local-cache control. Output token IDs match across all four phases and both arms (16 request outputs).

Raw records and checked summary: [`serial-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-before-jsonl), [`serial-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-after-jsonl), and [`serial-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-serial-comparison-json).

### Concurrent: uneven prefill chunks can eliminate CPU reuse

Submit both prompts together (`max_num_seqs=2`). They share the 64-token prefill budget with `long_prefill_token_threshold=63`, allowing uneven 63/1-token chunks. Each arm runs **cold → reset GPU cache only → CPU replay → GPU-hot control**. Each row below identifies a different prompt in the same concurrent batch.

| Prompt tokens | GPU-hot reuse, both arms | CPU replay before | CPU replay after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,257 | 8,064 | 8,064 | 8,064 |
| 8,321 | 8,192 | **0** | **8,192** |

The 8,257-token prompt is an unaffected control: its 8,064-token CPU hit already matches its full GPU-reusable prefix. The 8,321-token prompt reproduces the bug: CPU reuse is zero before the fix and reaches its full 8,192-token reusable prefix afterward.

CPU replay has **zero local GPU-cache hits** in both arms. Output token IDs match across all three phases and both arms (12 request outputs). The later GPU-hot control cannot warm the earlier CPU replay.

Raw records and checked summary: [`concurrent-before.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-before-jsonl), [`concurrent-after.jsonl`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-after-jsonl), and [`concurrent-comparison.json`](https://gist.github.com/SherifWaly/96dff7be8b847fd3fb5367628ecbc217#file-concurrent-comparison-json).

### Environment and additional checks

- **GPU environment:** 2× B200, driver 580.126.20; public image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e`; vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`. Only the two production files in this PR are patched in the fixed arm. They are identical at the image's source revision and the PR base `30d4032363d4a1f6412d9a235049673b41309f98`.
- **New CPU regression on the PR base:** baseline **12 failed / 6 passed**; patched **18 passed**, included in the **78/78** passing offload scheduler tests. The matrix covers replicated SWA, replicated full-attention, and sharded full-attention drafts; dense/latest-only retention; small/large chunks and multi-token prefill lookahead. It checks GPU/CPU hit equivalence and the loaded block hashes using real cache managers with simulated transfer completion.
- **Existing prefix-cache coverage:** **31 passed**, selecting EAGLE, cache publication, retention, and per-group DCP tests.
- **Code checks:** all applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy 3.10, and CI test tethering; the additional mypy 3.12 check and `git diff --check` passed.
- The added cases extend the existing offload scheduler suite already run by `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

The tables report one serial A/B and one concurrent A/B. They establish cache/transfer consistency, not trained-model accuracy or production throughput. Elapsed times include warmup effects and are not used to claim a speedup. Both cases exercise sharded MTP; replicated SWA is covered by the CPU matrix. A trained-model accuracy evaluation is not included.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Download the linked gist into a fresh directory for each case. This command selects the concurrent case:

```bash
mkdir -p models/tiny_mtp
cp config.json models/tiny_mtp/config.json
docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host \
  -e REPRO_CASE=concurrent \
  -v "$PWD:/repro" --entrypoint bash \
  vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:584c6bc58f76411936e0f22a37039e436019e155ae144c017b7eebbe2edc1d4e \
  -lc 'REPRO_ROOT=/repro bash /repro/run_in_container.sh'
```

For the serial case, run the same command in another fresh gist directory with `-e REPRO_CASE=serial`. It runs both CPU replays with a GPU-only reset before each. Each invocation uses a fresh container so the baseline starts from the stock package.

The measured run used this image through Enroot; the equivalent Docker launcher above has not itself been run. The scripts and comparison logic are the measured versions. No checkpoint download is required. The wrapper enables serialization for its own offline layout-inspection RPC and starts no HTTP server.

CPU commands run on the PR checkout (`GIST_DIR` points to the downloaded gist containing the upstream logging fixtures; dependencies and the public OPT-125M config used by the existing test fixture are already installed):

```bash
# Run with only regression.patch applied to reproduce the baseline failures.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k test_dcp_draft_offload_preserves_prefix --tb=short
# Baseline: 12 failed, 6 passed.

# Run with the full fix applied.
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$GIST_DIR" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  -p upstream_log_fixtures tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short
# 78 passed, including all 18 new cases.

PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q \
  -k 'eagle or cache_blocks or retention or per_group_dcp' --tb=short
# 31 passed, 140 deselected.
```

Code checks (with the three changed files staged):

```bash
uv --no-config tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run
uv --no-config tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run \
  mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py
git diff --check
```

</details>

## Details

Eager CPU selection currently rounds confirmed tokens to a common alignment. This can disagree with GPU cacheability in two ways:

1. Multi-module MTP keeps `num_prefill_lookahead - 1` trailing tokens re-prefillable. A block can fall inside the CPU scan before the GPU has hashed it. Selection skips it as not hashed but advances the persistent store cursor, so it is never revisited after finalization. A missing early block can collapse the reusable CPU prefix to zero.
2. Hybrid speculative lookup matches an extra draft block and then drops it. GPU publication already allows this block past the aligned boundary, but CPU selection truncates it away, losing otherwise reusable prefix length.

`get_num_cacheable_tokens()` extracts the existing GPU eligibility calculation. GPU publication and eager CPU selection now use it, including the per-group draft-block rule. The CPU coordinator also receives `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens`, so both sides agree on finalization. This adds no GPU synchronization and does not change model computation.

**Duplicate-work check:** #54736 fixes geometry/fine-grained offload support, not this speculative eligibility mismatch. #58413 changes align-mode Mamba chunks in the separate `OffloadingConnector`; #54979 concerns terminal GPU cache registration; #50897 proposes a broader successor-aware hash/publication protocol. None implements this `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` store-boundary fix. Searches for open SimpleCPU/speculative offload fixes found no equivalent PR.

**AI assistance was used** for implementation, tests, reproduction, and this description.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DiffusionGemma] Read the causal mask as int32 and compile the sample step
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59991. 

This PR has two fixes for DiffusionGemma. The first unblocks the CPU backend. The second applies to every platform.

1. DiffusionGemma fails on every CPU run. #51994 made the per-request causal mask `int32` and updated FlashAttention and Triton. CPU attention still reads it as `bool`. This PR makes the CPU kernel read `int32`.

2. #58226 left `_compiled_sample_step` uncompiled on every platform. This PR moves its `torch.compile` decorators back from the `_denoise_temperature` helper.

No open issue or PR covers either fix. For the causal mask I searched for the error message, `dynamic_causal` on CPU and DiffusionGemma on CPU. For the sample step I searched open PRs for `_compiled_sample_step`, `_denoise_temperature` and `58226`. The only hits, #45954, #47278 and #56210, do not touch the decorators.

## Claims

CPU causal mask (7b1cee8156):

- Fixes `RuntimeError: expected scalar type Bool but found Int` on the CPU backend. It is raised at engine startup. No DiffusionGemma request can run on CPU on `main`.
- CPU attention follows the `int32` contract from #51994. The mask is passed through without a cast, like FlashAttention, Triton and the XPU support in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57747.
- `test_cpu_attn.py` builds the mask as `int32`, like the model does. The existing per-request causal test reproduces the bug on `main`.

Sample step compile (c4a07b1796):

- `_compiled_sample_step` is compiled again, as it was before #58226. `_denoise_temperature` stays compiled and drops the raised recompile limit, which it does not need.
- On CPU, given the same random tokens, the compiled step matches the eager step. It is about 2x faster without self-conditioning and 1.0x to 1.5x faster with it. End-to-end CPU throughput is unchanged within noise.
- `test_sample_step_is_compiled` fails if `torch.compile` moves off the step again.

## Validation

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C (AMX), Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at 7867d6c52d.


### CPU causal mask

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_varlen_with_paged_kv_dynamic_causal` | 36 failed, `expected scalar type Bool but found Int` | 36 passed |
| `tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py` | | 1621 passed, 1153 skipped |
| DiffusionGemma structured read, `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` in BF16 | fails at startup with the same error | 3 runs of 50 reads, identical outputs |

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k dynamic_causal
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py
```

Any DiffusionGemma request on a CPU build reproduces it. I used `LLM.generate` with a structured read (32-token canvas, read-only, one step).

### Sample step compile

- `test_sample_step_is_compiled` fails before the change and passes after. Its module skips without CUDA and I have no GPU, so I called the test function directly on CPU.
- Compiled against eager over 16 combinations of canvas width, self-conditioning on or off, fp32 or bf16 embeddings, and peaked or flat logits, 6 steps each, with inductor's `fallback_random` on. Sampled tokens and state match. No graph breaks.

Sample step alone, vocab 262144, hidden 2816, bf16 embeddings, median of 10 calls. Eager is the same build under `torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager")`.

| requests x canvas | self-conditioning | eager | compiled | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 x 256 | off | 0.4 ms | 0.2 ms | 2.3x |
| 8 x 64 | off | 0.5 ms | 0.2 ms | 2.1x |
| 1 x 256 | on | 56.9 ms | 56.7 ms | 1.0x |
| 8 x 64 | on | 189.7 ms | 123.6 ms | 1.5x |

End to end with `LLM.generate`: `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` in BF16, `enforce_eager=True` (it does not turn off the step's own `torch.compile`), canvas 64, 8 chat prompts per call, `max_tokens=128`. 3 timed calls after a warmup, arms run in the order shown.

| arm | sample step | tokens (last call) | tok/s (median call) | per-call time (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (7b1cee8156) | eager | 769 | 16.45 | 49.8, 46.7, 40.2 |
| after (c4a07b1796) | compiled | 762 | 16.75 | 45.5, 48.2, 43.6 |
| before (7b1cee8156) | eager | 769 | 15.97 | 49.3, 48.2, 42.3 |

The difference is within run-to-run noise. On CPU the sample step is a small share of each call. The compiled arm words answers differently because the renoise tokens now come from inductor's RNG.

I couldn't test in GPU (running short today).

## Details


### CPU causal mask

#51994 fixed a FULL CUDA graph bug. FlashAttention cast the `bool` mask to `int32` on every `build()`, and the captured graph kept reading the tensor from capture time. The fix allocates the mask as `int32` in DiffusionGemma, and FlashAttention now rejects other dtypes. CPU attention passes the same tensor to its C++ ops, which read it with `data_ptr<bool>()`. The CPU tests built their own `bool` mask. CI stayed green.

The kernel reads `int32` instead of `CPUAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` casting the mask. A cast there would bring back the per-step allocation #51994 removed. It is harmless on CPU today, since CPU has no graph capture, but it would break the contract every other backend follows.

No measurable tradeoffs. The kernel reads the flag once per request and once per work group. The mask grows from 1 to 4 bytes per request.

Limitations:

- The CPU ops now reject `bool` masks. The only caller passes the model's `int32` mask.
- `test_varlen_with_paged_kv_dynamic_causal` runs only on CPUs with AMX. Other ISAs share the changed lines, but no test covers their per-request causal path, before or after this PR.

### Sample step compile

#58226 added `_denoise_temperature` directly below the `@torch._dynamo.config.patch(recompile_limit=64)` and `@torch.compile` decorators of `_compiled_sample_step`, and Python applied them to the helper. Since then the step has run eager on every platform. The step body has not changed since #58226. The fix restores the earlier layout.

Tradeoffs, each the same as before #58226:

- The renoise `torch.randint` uses inductor's RNG. At a given global seed, outputs differ from the eager step. Diffusion models reject per-request seeds.
- On CPU, warmup does not reach the sample step. Each new shape specialization compiles on first use while serving.

Limitations:

- No GPU numbers and no accuracy eval.
- `test_sample_step_is_compiled` checks `_torchdynamo_orig_callable`, which `test_batched_count_greater_than.py` also reads. Compiled and eager differ only in random draws, so no output assertion can tell them apart.


---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply model-default reasoning parser in GPU-less render server
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the GPU-less render server (`vllm launch render`) ignoring model-default reasoning parsers, which left gpt-oss (harmony) output completely unparsed by the derender endpoints. The same mis-resolution affected the render leg too: `OnlineRenderer` received the raw (empty) flag as well, so both the render and derender handlers now get the resolved value.

`init_render_app_state` passed the raw `--reasoning-parser` CLI flag to `OnlineRenderer`/`OnlineDerenderer`, missing model-specific defaults applied by `verify_and_update_config` (e.g. `"openai_gptoss"` for `gpt_oss`, set in `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`). The main API server uses the config-resolved value (`vllm/entrypoints/generate/api_router.py`), so the two frontends diverged.

The render entrypoint builds `VllmConfig(model_config=...)` directly, bypassing `create_engine_config` — so the CLI flag was never merged into `structured_outputs_config` there. The fix extracts that merge into `EngineArgs.create_structured_outputs_config()` (called from both `create_engine_config` and the render entrypoint), and `app_state` reads the config-resolved value with `args.reasoning_parser` kept as the first source, so callers that construct a `VllmConfig` without the merge still honor an explicit flag.

Note: `create_structured_outputs_config` also merges `--reasoning-parser-plugin` for `create_engine_config` parity, but that part is inert for the render server (plugin import happens from `args` in the launcher and already worked); no behavior change is claimed for it.

Observable impact before this fix, with `vllm launch render openai/gpt-oss-20b` (no flags):

- `ParserManager.get_parser` received no parser names and returned `None` before its `is_harmony` check.
- Non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` returned raw harmony markup as `content` (e.g. `"analysisNeed the weather for Paris.assistantfinalIt is sunny."`) — no `reasoning`, no `tool_calls`.
- Streaming derender leaked the raw markup into `delta.content` instead of failing closed (whether channel markers appear as literal special-token text additionally depends on the request's `skip_special_tokens` and the tokenizer's special-token flags).

After the fix, the same launch parses harmony like the main server (`reasoning`/`content` split correctly), and streaming fails closed with the documented 501 until parser-aware streaming derender (#50550) lands — the two changes compose (verified on that PR's branch).

**Not a duplicate:** searched open/closed PRs and issues for render/derender + harmony/gpt-oss/reasoning-parser combinations; nothing addresses this. #50550 (streaming parse path) is orthogonal and does not touch parser-name resolution.

No model-output changes: this affects only frontend prompt/response processing parity, so no model evals are applicable.

## Test Plan

Regression unit tests (real gpt-oss `VllmConfig`, heavy constructors monkeypatched) and flag-precedence coverage:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/render/ -q
```

E2E regression on a no-flag gpt-oss render server (new), plus existing suites guarding the flagged paths (the DeepSeek-R1 e2e tests launch a real server with `--reasoning-parser` and assert parsed reasoning):

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -q
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -q
```

Lint:

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/engine/arg_utils.py vllm/entrypoints/launchers/render/entry.py vllm/entrypoints/launchers/render/app_state.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/entrypoints/launchers/render/app_state.py --hook-stage manual
```

## Test Result

- Unit regression fails on unfixed code with `AssertionError: assert '' == 'openai_gptoss'`; passes with the fix. Flag-precedence test confirms an explicit `--reasoning-parser` survives `VllmConfig` construction over the model default.
- New `test_e2e_harmony_reasoning_default_parser` (bare gpt-oss server, no parser flags) passes: reasoning parsed, no `<|channel|>` markup in `content`.
- Full render/derender/launcher suites pass; all pre-commit hooks incl. CI-style `mypy-3.12` pass.
- Manual e2e: non-streaming derender returns `reasoning: 'Need the weather for Paris.'` / `content: 'It is sunny.'` (previously raw markup); streaming returns HTTP 501 fail-closed.

## AI-assisted contribution

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, who ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CPU][Recipes] Detect model head constraints for automatic tensor parallel selection in vLLM Recipes Tool
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make automatic CPU recipe TP selection consider model attention and KV head counts alongside NUMA topology. This prevents incompatible suggestions such as TP=4 for `microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning`, which requires TP=2 under the current power-of-two policy.

## Claims

- Detect head constraints from the effective model configuration without loading model weights or maintaining a fixed model table.
- Select the largest compatible power-of-two TP within the effective NUMA-node count, including supported KV-head replication.
- Check nested text, global attention, Whisper encoder/decoder, hybrid linear-attention, and vision head constraints.
- Preserve recipe parallelism when detection fails or DP/PP is greater than 1, with explanatory tuning notes.

## Validation

Focused synthetic configuration checks passed for:

- Phi-4 reasoning: 40 attention heads and 10 KV heads reduce TP=4 to TP=2.
- Compatible GQA and KV replication: retain TP=8.
- Additional vision and hybrid constraints: reduce incompatible candidates.
- Whisper encoder/decoder extraction and exclusion of vision constraints when the encoder uses data parallelism.

Reproduce the Phi-4 selection check:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=tools/recipes python3 - <<'PY'
from model_constraints import HeadConstraint, suggest_tensor_parallel_size

constraints = (HeadConstraint("text", 40, 10),)
assert suggest_tensor_parallel_size(4, constraints) == 2
print("PASS: Phi-4 reasoning TP=4 -> TP=2")
PY
```

Full CPU serving and weekly catalog validation remain pending. This change adds no automated test files.

## Details

Previously, automatic TP selection used only the effective NUMA-node count. A topology-compatible value can still fail model head partitioning: Phi-4 reasoning’s 10 KV heads cannot be evenly distributed across four TP ranks.

The new `model_constraints.py` reads configuration through vLLM’s loader, honoring model revisions, remote-code settings, config format, and JSON `hf-overrides`. Candidates must divide attention heads and either partition KV heads evenly or support their replication. Incompatible candidates are halved until all detected constraints pass.

Automatic TP selection applies only when DP=1 and PP=1. Automatic DP tuning remains disabled; related CPU binding work is discussed in [[#47328](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47328)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47328) and [[#47336](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47336)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47336).

If detection fails, the recipe TP is retained rather than certified as compatible. Plain conversion without hardware detection does not fetch model configuration. Head checks do not establish memory fit or complete backend support; vLLM still validates the final configuration at startup.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Pass tool defer_loading through to chat templates
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Pass the tool `defer_loading` flag through the Rust frontend's Chat Completions path to HF chat templates, matching the Python frontend (#40190).

## Claims

- `tools[].defer_loading` and `tools[].function.defer_loading` are both accepted; the function-level value wins, same as Python's `ChatCompletionToolsParam._propagate_defer_loading`.
- HF templates see `tools[i].function.defer_loading` when it is set and nothing when it is unset, matching Python's `FunctionDefinition` serializer, so `is defined` checks behave the same.
- Before this change the Rust DTO silently dropped the field, so templates that render deferred tools differently (for example name + description only) got full schemas instead, and the prompt differed from the Python frontend's without any error.
- Parsers, output grammars, and tool-choice validation ignore the flag, so deferred tools stay callable, as in Python.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server`: 1377/1377 pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `pre-commit` pass.
- Tests:
  - New `prepare_chat_request_maps_tool_defer_loading`: the tool-level value propagates, and the function-level value takes precedence.
  - Extended `chat_template_preserves_python_optional_tool_fields`: a template iterating `tool.function.items()` sees `defer_loading=true` when it is set and no key when it is unset, the same field set Python's `FunctionDefinition.model_dump()` produces.
- Additionally checked locally with a chat template that renders deferred tools as name + description only: the Rust `HfChatRenderer` output is byte-identical to Python `transformers` rendering of the same request.

## Details

- `defer_loading` is not an OpenAI Chat Completions field; it comes from tool search in the OpenAI Responses API and in Anthropic Messages. The Python frontend accepts it on Chat Completions as an extension and only passes it through to the template, with no server-side search; this PR brings the Rust frontend to the same behavior.
- The field goes on the shared `vllm_parser::tool::Tool` (`ChatTool`) next to `strict`, which is also template-visible. Most of the diff is mechanical `defer_loading: None` in existing struct literals; the logic change is about 15 lines.
- Not duplicating existing work: no open PR covers this. The open Rust Anthropic Messages PR #52896 accepts and drops `AnthropicTool.defer_loading` because "the Rust chat layer has no analog for it"; this PR adds that analog, so the Anthropic path can forward the flag in a follow-up.
- Out of scope: `tool_reference` content parts (#40190), which mainly serve the Anthropic → Chat translation; and namespace tools (#47024), which exist only in the Responses API.

commits.pr_title: [Model] LongCat-Flash: scale MLA norms while loading and drop the post-load sweep
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

LongCat-Flash's `load_weights` ends with a post-processing sweep. It block-dequantizes `kv_b_proj` into `w_kc` / `w_vc`, which nothing reads, and scales the MLA LoRA norms in place behind once-only flags. This PR removes the sweep and scales the norms in their weight loaders. It also fixes the MTP-weight skip in the target loader, without which LongCat-Flash-Chat cannot load. It is a prerequisite for #57733: `load_weights` now only loads.

## Claims

- LongCat-Flash-Chat-FP8 gives correct output: GSM8K 0.000 → 0.916. On `main` its MLA LoRA norms end up unscaled because the post-load sweep runs before they are loaded (details below).
- LongCat-Flash-Chat-FP8 loads again. The target loader skipped MTP weights with `".mtp." in name`, but `AutoWeightsLoader` strips the `model.` prefix, so the names are `mtp.layers.…` and loading fails with `KeyError: 'mtp.layers.0.hnorm.m.weight'`.
- `reload_weights` keeps the MLA LoRA norms scaled. On `main` the `_mla_*_lora_scaled` flags survive the reload, so the reloaded norms stay unscaled and accuracy collapses.
- `reload_weights` no longer crashes for FP8 checkpoints with quantized attention (LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8): the removed `block_dequant` of `kv_b_proj` asserts on the reloaded shard.
- Removes dead code: `w_kc` / `w_vc` are written and never read; `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading` derives `W_UK_T` / `W_UV` from `kv_b_proj` itself. The removed block also left `w` unbound for FP8 with `weight_block_size=None`; no public LongCat checkpoint reaches that branch.

## Validation

GB200, real weights, `vllm serve`, `--enforce-eager` (see below). GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. "Control" is the image's LongCat loader (same sweep and flags as `main`) plus only the MTP-prefix fix, so that Chat can load at all.

| model, parallelism | control: GSM8K → `reload_weights` → GSM8K | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| LongCat-Flash-Chat-FP8, DP2 × TP4, EP8 (2 nodes) | **0.000** (norms left unscaled, see below) → 0.000 | 0.916 → 0.914 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite (BF16), TP4, EP | 0.841 → **0.036** | 0.846 → 0.844 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8, TP4, EP | 0.834 → **reload fails** (`block_dequant`: `assert n_tiles == x_s.shape[0]`) | 0.839 → 0.843 |
| LongCat-Flash-Chat-FP8 + MTP k=1 (control: this PR's target with `main`'s MTP): GSM8K, draft acceptance, after reload | 0.912, 92.4%, 0.916 | 0.909, 92.5%, 0.911 |

`pre-commit` passes.

Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this change, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates. On this image `torch.compile` fails for LongCat on both arms (a Dynamo data-dependent assert in the zero-expert path, `moe_runner._maybe_add_zero_expert_output`), hence `--enforce-eager`; the change is load-time only.

## Details

**Why Chat-FP8 scores 0 on `main`.** `AutoWeightsLoader` calls `FlashModel.load_weights` once per contiguous run of `model.*` names. LongCat-Flash-Chat-FP8 streams 16 `model.*` tensors, then `lm_head`, then the remaining 73046, so the sweep runs at the end of the first call: it scales the norms before they are loaded and sets the flags. The second call loads the real norms, and the flags skip the scaling. A debug build shows layer 0's `q_a_layernorm` summing to 1892.8 on `main` and 3785.6 with this PR (the expected factor √(6144/1536) = 2), and `kv_a_layernorm` 6.74 vs 23.34 (√(6144/512) ≈ 3.46).

**Norm scaling.** `scale_mla_lora_norms_on_load` sets the `weight_loader` of `q_a_layernorm.weight` / `kv_a_layernorm.weight` to `composed_weight_loader(default_weight_loader, lambda x: x * factor)` when the config enables the scaling (the same pattern as plamo3). Every load, including a reload, writes checkpoint × factor, so no flag is needed. It is applied to both attention modules of each decoder layer and to the MTP block.

**MTP skip.** `FlashModel.load_weights` now skips names starting with `mtp.` once, at the top of the loop, instead of three `".mtp." in name` checks that never matched. `LongCatFlashMTP` loads those weights.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes these loaders. #53811 proposes removing the native LongCat implementation in favour of the Transformers backend; it is not merged and has conflicts. This PR fixes the native implementation while it exists.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

commits.pr_title: [Feat][Mamba2] Enable internal prefill checkpoints
commits.pr_body:
> **Note from @ZJY0516:** I rewrote this description and made the code changes on this branch since the original revision:
> - `ab289e9bc3`: Mamba2 gets its own checkpoint store kernel, and the shared-exporter refactor is dropped.
> - `6ed5c4bce5`: drops tests that did not cover this change.
> - `dac3aa469a`: the Granite4 tool parser test fix.

## Purpose

Bring Kimi-K3's internal prefill checkpoints (#52789, #53614) to Mamba2 (NemotronH, Granite-4.0-H, Falcon-H1, Zamba2).

In `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the scheduler currently splits a prefill so one step ends on a block boundary, which costs an extra forward pass. With this PR, the whole prompt runs in one step and the boundary state is read out of the SSD scan's per-chunk states.

## Changes

- `_compute_chunk_metadata` splits a checkpointing request at the checkpoint, so a logical chunk ends exactly there, and returns that chunk's index.
- Checkpoint positions come from the existing `MambaPrefillCheckpointBuilder`, so the scheduler, `MambaManager` and backends agree on which rows checkpoint. The only addition is an optional host copy of the offsets, which avoids a GPU→CPU sync when laying out chunks.
- A small Triton kernel (`ops/ssd_checkpoint.py`) writes the conv window and the checkpoint SSM state into the paged cache in one launch. Rows that decline are masked off, so there is no sync. KDA/GLM code is untouched.
- `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder.update_block_table` re-gathers checkpoint blocks per KV cache group, as #59536 does for GDN. Both model runners reuse metadata across groups. Without this, every group wrote into the first group's block, and 20-shot GSM8K dropped to 0.02.
- `test_granite4_tool_parser.py` now runs with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. The test requires a non-streaming and a streaming greedy run of the same prompt to match bitwise.
  - On main, both runs prefill the tail after the block boundary in a separate forward pass, so their numerics are identical.
  - With this PR, the first run prefills the tail in the same pass as the head, while the second resumes from the checkpoint. The tail tokens then go through different attention/MoE batch shapes, and on H200 a near-tied token flipped.
  - The test targets the tool parser, not prefix caching. The same applies to Kimi-K3's and GLM-5.3-Flash's internal checkpoints: a prefix-cache hit is no longer bitwise identical to a cold prefill.

## Test Result

Unit/kernel tests:

- `test_mamba2_checkpoint_state.py`, `test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py`: 12 passed.
- Mamba/GDN/KDA metadata and align chunk-split tests: 138 passed.
- `test_granite4_tool_parser.py`: passed locally on GB200, with and without prefix caching.

E2E: 1x GB200, TP1, CUDA graphs, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, A/B against main.

**GSM8K, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 (1319 questions)**

| | main (MRV2) | PR (MRV2) | PR (MRV1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5-shot | 0.8544 | 0.8544 | 0.8552 |
| 20-shot | 0.8681 | 0.8666 | 0.8673 |
| 40-shot + MTP×3 | 0.8628 | 0.8658 | – |

- 20-shot prompts (~4.1k tokens) take and resume from checkpoints.
- With MTP, EAGLE block drop leaves 20-shot prompts with no prefix-cache hit, so the MTP run uses 40-shot (hit rate 53.6% on both arms).

Granite-4.0-H-Small, 20-shot: main 0.8506, PR 0.8476.

**TTFT, Lightning, random 8000 in / 1000 out**

| Concurrency | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 143.3 ms | 95.3 ms | −33% |
| 4 | 246.5 ms | 205.8 ms | −17% |
| 16 | 549.3 ms | 461.4 ms | −16% |

TPOT and throughput are unchanged.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR targets Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints (searched 2026-10-05).

- This PR builds on #57783 and #59536.
- #58851 (open) shares Mamba metadata across groups on MRV2; whichever PR lands second has to carry the Mamba2 checkpoint re-gather.
- #60050 does the same for GDN on FlashInfer and adds the same `offsets` field.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCM][Perf] Add ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN attention-backend works across RDNA3/3.5/4
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` attention backend with segmented Triton attention for paged decode, prefill, and multi-token verification. Startup tuning persists launch choices and shares a Triton cache across target and draft compilation.

- Supports RDNA3, RDNA3.5, and RDNA4 (gfx11/gfx12) with native FP16/BF16 KV; FP8 KV is gated to gfx12.
- Covers head sizes 64, 128, and 256, GQA ratios 1–16, causal and non-causal attention, sliding windows, and attention sinks.
- Includes focused kernel, backend-selection, workspace, tuning-cache, and Triton-cache tests.
- Uses the existing Triton/ROCm stack and adds no package dependency or custom compiler build.
- Startup autotuning is disabled by default to avoid the tuning sweep during engine startup. Set `--kernel-config.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune=True` to enable it; skipping tuning may reduce serving performance.

## Relationship to existing work

This overlaps with [#55996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55996), which adds generalized Triton SplitKV paged decode plus an optional RDNA4 FlyDSL path.The overlap is in terms of paged attention optimization. That optional path requires a custom FlyDSL build. `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` uses Triton already in vLLM, with no additional dependency, and covers paged decode, prefill, and multi-token verification across gfx11/gfx12. It also covers D=64, sliding windows, and attention sinks. The serving results below compare against `ROCM_ATTN`; they are not a direct performance comparison with #55996.

## Validation

The three serving comparisons used ROCm 10, the same PyTorch version, and the same GuideLLM 0.7.3 `simple-agent-multiturn-prefix-cache` workload. Each run used eight turns, 2,048 configured prompt tokens per turn, 512 output tokens per request, seed `20260715`, and 1/2/4/8 configured streams with 8/16/32/64 completed requests, respectively. All runs finished with zero errors or incomplete requests.

Each table compares `ROCM_ATTN` (baseline) with `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` (candidate). Values are arithmetic means across successful requests; output tokens/s is **per-request**. These are end-to-end serving measurements, including model execution and scheduling, rather than isolated kernel timings. Hardware, model, and serving options are listed for each comparison.

### gfx1151 serving comparison

On gfx1151, the comparison used `dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound`.

![gfx1201 per-turn end-to-end latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm/74e0566533ec61d5c73d0a1b92cc94fc0e750a09/gfx1201/compare_e2e_by_turn.png)

Candidate serving command; the baseline used the same options with `--attention-backend ROCM_ATTN`:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-model-len auto \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --load-format safetensors \
    --attention-backend ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN
```

Both measured runs used `--load-format safetensors`; the supplied `fastsafetensors` launcher failed to start in this environment.

## Speculative decoding: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + DFlash2 on gfx1201

Measured on two Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs (TP2), using `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, seven speculative tokens, FP8 KV, and concurrency 4. Both the target and draft use the backend selected for each case:

- **A:** `ROCM_ATTN`.
- **B:** `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN`, autotuning disabled.
- **C:** `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN`, autotuning enabled.

### Accuracy checks first

GSM8K uses the same first 100 test questions and five worked training examples in every case. Sampling follows the model's thinking-mode recommendation: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0, presence penalty 0, repetition penalty 1, and default `xhigh` reasoning effort. Each question uses a fixed seed.

| Case | GSM8K correct / 100 |
| --- | ---: |
| A: baseline | 98 |
| B: segmented, static | 98 |
| C: segmented, tuned — pass 1 | 99 |
| C: segmented, tuned — pass 2 | 98 |

A/B miss IDs 12 and 45; C misses ID 12 in pass 1 and IDs 12 and 45 in pass 2. C repeats the same 100 questions, rather than adding 100 new evaluation questions. This is a quick quality check, not a full canonical GSM8K evaluation.

The long-context inputs are **coherent GSM8K worked problems**, followed by a new question; no random-token prompts are used. Actual input lengths are 16,606–16,636 and 32,817–32,847 tokens, with four requests at each length. These speed checks use a **512-token output cap**:

| Input | A correct / 4 | B correct / 4 | C correct / 4, passes 1 / 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16K | 3 | 3 | 3 / 3 |
| 32K | 3 | 3 | 3 / 3 |

The small sample and truncated outputs make the long-context results a serving check, not an accuracy claim.

### A → B: speculative-decoding speed with segmented attention

The backend covers multi-token verification and non-causal draft attention. The PR also reserves attention scratch space before graph capture, initializes draft attention in its own workspace lane, and preserves a shared Triton cache across target/draft compilation.

| Workload | A: baseline output tokens/s | B: segmented static output tokens/s | B / A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, 100 questions | 102.27 | **253.50** | **2.48×** |
| 16K coherent input, 4 requests | 8.20 | **185.47** | **22.62×** |
| 32K coherent input, 4 requests | 4.08 | **131.54** | **32.27×** |

These are **aggregate final output tokens/s**, calculated as returned completion tokens divided by batch wall time, including prefill and scheduling and excluding warmup and draft proposals. They differ from the **per-request** GuideLLM rates in the earlier tables.

Mean acceptance length (`1 + accepted draft tokens / draft rounds`) was approximately **4.05 → 4.05** for GSM8K, **1.04 → 3.92** at 16K, and **1.03 → 3.90** at 32K. The large long-context gains coincide with recovering draft acceptance from near one token per round in A. Both target and draft backends change, so this does not isolate a single kernel or establish the cause of the baseline acceptance collapse. The 22–32× figures describe this specific DFlash2 workload, not a general serving speedup.

### B → C: additional performance with autotuning

The tuner selects launch configurations for the target and draft attention workloads. Updated C uses the original C run's saved **125 target and 42 draft** tuning records, unchanged, with two warmed measured passes.

| Workload | B: static output tokens/s | C: tuned mean output tokens/s | C passes 1 / 2 | Observed C vs B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, 100 questions | 253.50 | **268.79** | 261.97 / 275.62 | **+6.0%** |
| 16K coherent input, 4 requests | 185.47 | **195.80** | 186.04 / 205.56 | **+5.6%** |
| 32K coherent input, 4 requests | 131.54 | **134.64** | 135.35 / 133.94 | **+2.4%** |

C is the arithmetic mean of both batch rates. These results suggest additional serving benefit from autotuning, but **A/B are historical single runs and C uses extended warmup plus prefix-cache resets**. The smaller B/C differences are observed comparisons, not an isolated or statistically established autotuning gain.

### First engine startup cost

Autotuning adds work on the **first startup with an empty matching tuning cache**:

| Configuration | Tuning time | Engine initialization time | Extra initialization vs B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B: autotuning disabled | — | 253.88 s | — |
| C: cold autotuning (separate startup measurement) | 410.02 s target + 88.44 s draft | 750.34 s | **496.46 s (~8.3 min)** |

These are logged engine initialization times (profiling, KV allocation, and model warmup), not full process launch-to-ready times. Matching cached startups loaded all 167 records and tuned zero workloads, avoiding the tuning sweep; model loading, compilation, and graph capture still have their own costs. Cache invalidation can require retuning. Set `--kernel-config.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune=False` to skip tuning.

### Speculative-decoding serving commands

Run one server at a time on the two-GPU setup above. These commands select the attention backend for **both the target and the DFlash2 draft**, with seven speculative tokens.

**A — baseline (`ROCM_ATTN`):**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --load-format safetensors \
    --attention-backend ROCM_ATTN \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"ROCM_ATTN"}'
```

**C — segmented attention with autotuning enabled:**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --max-num-seqs 4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --load-format safetensors \
    --attention-backend ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN \
    --kernel-config.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune=True \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN"}'
```

For **B — segmented attention without autotuning**, omit the autotuning flag from the second command (the current default is disabled). Python callers enable tuning with `kernel_config={"enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune": True}`. The setting follows the existing FlashInfer autotuning pattern in `KernelConfig` and applies per engine to startup tuning, workspace sizing, and tuned-kernel selection.

The measured runs used cached model snapshots: target `017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a` and draft `50307d4c4cde6860d4eee73e2547cd786fe8e8a4`. For exact model-weight reproduction, substitute the corresponding local snapshot paths for the model IDs. Sampling settings and client concurrency are supplied by the benchmark client.

### Reproducibility and validation scope

- Serving settings: `--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --load-format safetensors`; seven DFlash2 speculative tokens. A/B disable autotuning; C enables autotuning explicitly in the current API. The historical measurements used the former environment variable; the commands above use the current KernelConfig API.
- PR Python source at `2f2ccc82515537f3a1add4d547b5aae60527fc76` was copied into the same ROCm 10 image, retaining compiled extensions from `4f20819329`. C uses the source now committed as `0eb508cf96811c8c2b4f5d057305fb6aa5fa704c`. This is not a clean image build from the PR head.
- Before C's measurements, each server warmed four full GSM8K requests and both long workloads. Prefix caches were reset before each batch, followed by the client's excluded 128-token warmup. A's historical 16K run had an extra cached prefix from an exploratory run, favoring its prefill.
- To hold tuning choices fixed across the source change, only the tuner-source hash in the saved cache identity was adapted; all launch records and the attention-kernel source hash were verified unchanged.
- **20 focused tuning tests passed** (58 deselected). Repository pre-commit checks passed. The full focused suite suggested below has not been rerun.

Command used inside the GPU test container (PR worktree mounted at `/src`):

```bash

    -k tuning --confcutdir=/src/tests/kernels/attention -q
```

### Source and test checks

- A previous independent checkout reported 83 passing focused segmented, cache, and workspace tests; these have not been rerun on the squashed commit.
- After syncing to current `main` and squashing to one commit, `git diff --check`, Ruff lint, and Ruff format checks pass on all 14 changed Python files. The final PR diff contains only source and tests.
- The full focused suite has not been rerun in this checkout. The GPU-container tuning tests and GSM8K/DFlash2 evaluations are recorded in the speculative-decoding section above. Earlier serving measurements from a separate combined RDNA4 stack are excluded from this standalone-branch result.

Suggested focused run before marking ready:

```bash

```

### KernelConfig migration validation (2026-10-04)

On ROCm 10 / gfx1201, using the native `rocm_workspaces/10/gfx1201` environment against the PR review checkout:

- 100 focused segmented-attention kernel and backend cases passed; 62 unrelated cases were deselected. Existing tests were adapted to the new setting; no configuration-only tests were added.
- Qwen3-0.6B eager generation with default-on tuning and explicit opt-out returned identical eight-token output. Default-on tuned ten workloads with zero failures; opt-out skipped startup tuning. This is a startup/generation smoke check, not a model-quality benchmark.
- Python configuration, dotted CLI and JSON CLI forms passed. Ruff lint, formatting and configuration validation passed.

```bash
    tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py -k segmented -q
```

The review checkout reused native compiled extensions from the gfx1201 workspace; only Python source changed. Existing serving and model-quality results above remain historical measurements.

### Shared kernel warmup migration (2026-10-04)

Segmented attention tuning now lives in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/rocm_segmented_attn_autotune_warmup.py` and is invoked by `kernel_warmup()` after KV allocation and before live graph capture. The post-load hook only retains each layer's engine configuration. Workload selection still respects target/draft model length and query limits; temporary scratch uses remaining free memory, while cache feasibility uses the allocated KV-cache budget. The `KernelConfig.enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune` setting now defaults to `False` following maintainer review and can be enabled with the CLI/Python options above. The moved source changes the tuning-cache identity, so old records will be regenerated.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Use group-local ranks for torch P2P transfers
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With pipeline parallelism, EPLB passes EP-group-local peer ranks to its
communicators, but the torch NCCL and Gloo backends pass them as `P2POp.peer`,
which is a global rank. For an EP group containing global ranks `[2, 3]`,
local peer `1` is therefore interpreted as global rank `1`, outside the group,
and expert-weight transfer fails.

Use `group=...` and `group_peer=...` for both send and receive in the two
torch.distributed communicators. Add a transfer regression covering PP=1 and
PP=2 with two ranks per EP group and both backends.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-08 found no matching open PR in searches for
`EPLB`, `EPLB P2POp`, and `group_peer`. The related explicit EP topology PR
#52099 does not modify this communicator file.

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation, regression, and local
validation. Backend and model validation were performed by the PR author.

## Test Plan

On a configured vLLM environment with four GPUs:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py \
  -k test_eplb_communicator_pipeline_parallel -q
```

The regression exchanges rank-tagged tensors within each two-rank EP group
and checks the received values against the global rank of the expected peer.
The four-rank case covers the nonzero-rank group `[2, 3]`.

## Test Result

The author validated EPLB with pipeline parallelism using both `torch_gloo`
and `torch_nccl`:

- Before the fix, both backends raised the following error:

  ```text
  ValueError: Global rank {global_rank} is not part of group {group}
  ```

- After the fix, tests completed successfully with both backends.
- Model evaluation after the fix: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B**, using the **Gloo**
  backend, achieved **96.51% GSM8K accuracy**.

Additional local checks:

- Supplemental local CPU validation with PyTorch 2.14.0: both communicator
  classes were loaded from the production source and exercised with real Gloo
  process groups and real `P2POp`/`batch_isend_irecv`. Only CUDA stream contexts
  and synchronization were replaced with CPU no-ops; the NCCL class also used
  Gloo transport, so this is not NCCL device-transport validation.
- Before the fix, both classes fail in group `[2, 3]` with
  `Global rank 0/1 is not part of group`; the two-rank PP=1 controls pass.
  After the fix, all four combinations of communicator and world size (2, 4)
  transfer the expected tensor values successfully.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint and format checks, Python compilation, and
  `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py`: all applicable hooks passed with
  the Python 3.12 virtual environment on `PATH`.
- Native pytest command above: blocked during collection by missing `tblib`
  in the local macOS environment. The backend and GSM8K results above come
  from the author's separate test environment.

commits.pr_title: fix: exclude flashinfer-jit-cache from wheel install_requires
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`setup.py` excludes `flashinfer-cubin` from `install_requires` because it is only published on the FlashInfer custom wheel index (`https://flashinfer.ai/whl`), not on PyPI. However, `flashinfer-jit-cache` — which is hosted on the same custom index — is not excluded.

The Dockerfile already installs `flashinfer-jit-cache` separately from the custom index:

```dockerfile
uv pip install --system flashinfer-jit-cache==${FLASHINFER_VERSION} \
    --index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl/cu...
```

If `flashinfer-jit-cache` is added to `requirements/cuda.txt` (e.g. for pre-compiled JIT cache support), it would leak into the wheel metadata and make the published wheel uninstallable without the custom index configured:

```
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
  cause: Because there is no version of flashinfer-jit-cache==X.Y.Z
         and vllm depends on flashinfer-jit-cache==X.Y.Z, ...
```

## Fix

Extend the existing `flashinfer-cubin` exclusion in `setup.py` to also cover `flashinfer-jit-cache`, keeping wheel metadata free of custom-index-only dependencies.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Two tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py` asserted incorrect contracts and gave false confidence:

1. `test_enable_auto_choice_fails_with_enable_reasoning` claimed that combining `--enable-auto-tool-choice` with `--reasoning-parser` must fail. However, this combination is **documented as supported** in `docs/features/tool_calling.md` (e.g. `--tool-call-parser hunyuan_a13b --reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b`), and `validate_parsed_serve_args` correctly does **not** reject it. The test only passed because `--tool-call-parser` was omitted, so it actually triggered the unrelated "auto tool choice requires a tool call parser" check — masking that no reasoning-conflict validation exists (and none should). Rewritten to verify the documented combination passes when a tool call parser is set.

2. `test_enable_auto_choice_passes_without_tool_call_parser` was misnamed: its docstring and body assert that validation *fails*. Renamed to `test_enable_auto_choice_fails_without_tool_call_parser` to match its actual behavior.

This is a test-only change; no runtime behavior is modified.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for `test_cli_args`, `validate_parsed_serve_args`, and `test_enable_auto_choice` — none touch these tests.
