commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Enable OAI Triton MXFP4 MoE on SM12x
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Disclaimer: The code was largely assisted by Claude Code but the PR itself is handwritten and well tested.

In general, this PR is a follow-up to #41028.

#41028 tries to allow sm120 to use Triton kernels for GPT-OSS models instead of Marlin kernels. However, current implementation of triton kernels does not work on sm12x out-of-box and this PR fixes this. By testing on an RTX 5090:

- Decode speed is the same.
- Triton prefilling is 10% slower than Marlin kernels.The root cause is that the smem is too small for a larger tile for Triton. 
- Triton kernel earns +8% kvcache pool because Marlin kernel needs more space for alignment.

Therefore, this PR still keeps Marlin kernel as the default implementation, but allows sm12x to use Trition kernels if users would like the kvcache benefits by `--moe-backend triton`.

cc @Harry-Chen 

## Test Plan

CI, unit test.

## Test Result

See above.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Remove the PyO3 tool-parser bridge
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The PyO3 bridge to the Rust tool parsers (`vllm._rust_tool_parser`, added in vllm-project/vllm#44624) exposes only the Rust `ToolParser` over plain text. The Rust parsers have moved on (attributed `DecodedText` input, unified parsers, reasoning state), and the bridge cannot express is-reasoning-ended, so keeping it aligned costs more than it is worth. The next interface change, `ToolParser` taking attributed input for token-aware markers, would otherwise also need a text-only mode just for the bridge.

This PR removes the bridge. It is stacked on the previous PR, which moves its last production user, `minimax_m3`, to the parser engine.

## Claims

- Removes the `vllm-tool-parser-py` crate, `vllm/tool_parsers/rust_tool_parser.py` and its tests, the `RustExtension` entry, the `pyo3` / `pythonize` workspace dependencies, and the CI step that provided a shared-library Python for the crate's tests.
- Keeps the PyO3 build plumbing (`tools/build_rust.py`, `setup.py`, Dockerfiles) for a future `vllm._rust_*` module, with the removed `RustExtension` left as a commented example.

## Validation

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked` and `cargo sort --workspace --check` pass; `Cargo.lock` loses only `pyo3*`, `pythonize`, `target-lexicon`, and the crate itself.
- `pytest tests/tool_parsers tests/parser/engine`: no new failures (the remaining ones are pre-existing in this environment: gated Hugging Face models).
- The `uv run` script tests still run without the PyO3 environment, e.g. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding`.
- Not verified locally: the Docker image builds. `COPY --from=rust-build .../_rust_*.so vllm/` now matches no files, which relies on BuildKit accepting an empty wildcard; the image build in CI needs to confirm this.

## Details

- `setup.py`: with no PyO3 module configured, `has_precompiled_rust_extensions()` was vacuously true, which selected the precompiled `build_rust` command on every source build and logged a misleading "falling back to local Rust build" warning. It now returns false when there is no module to look for.
- CI: `setup_pyo3_python` is removed because nothing in the workspace links Python anymore. `uv` stays, and `install_uv` still installs a Python (`UV_SCRIPT_PYTHON_VERSION`, default 3.12), for the `uv run` script tests (`python_compat.py`, `grammar_replay.py`).
- Supersedes the draft vllm-project/vllm#50575 (unified-parser bridge) and makes vllm-project/vllm#51550 (bridge streaming flush) moot.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Port the `minimax_m3` tool parser from the PyO3 bridge to the Rust tool parser (`RustToolParser` → `vllm._rust_tool_parser`) onto the declarative parser engine. It is the bridge's only production user; the follow-up PR in this stack removes the bridge.

## Claims

- `minimax_m3` tool calling no longer needs the `vllm._rust_tool_parser` extension. Output is unchanged for well-formed model output in non-streaming and streaming paths, including nested object and array arguments.
- Request handling matches the bridge: required and named `tool_choice` still parse the native M3 syntax instead of forcing JSON, and `skip_special_tokens` is left as is.
- Malformed or truncated tool calls now follow the engine convention: the call is kept with the parameters parsed before the error. The bridge instead returned the raw text (non-streaming) or dropped the rest of the stream (streaming).

## Validation

- New `tests/parser/engine/test_minimax_m3.py` (17 cases: schema-driven nesting, empty containers, mixed text, malformed elements, depth limit, tool-block boundaries, streaming); M3 added to the trace-builder scenarios so `test_delegating_replay.py` replays it at every chunk size. Each of 8 mutations of the implementation (schema lookup, array handling, empty containers, depth cap, argument streaming, content stripping, `adjust_request`, `supports_required_and_named`) fails at least one test.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m3_tool_parser.py` passes unchanged except for the two assertions on the bridge's internal `streamed_args_for_tool` / `prev_tool_call_arr`, which now compare against the expected arguments; one regression test was added for required `tool_choice`.
- Differential check against the bridge built from current `main` Rust sources, using the real `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` tokenizer and chat template: outputs rendered by the template (nested objects, lists of objects, nested lists, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`, empty `[]` / `{}`, multiple invokes, unknown tools) plus hand-written edge cases, fed non-streaming, token by token, and in random character chunks. All well-formed inputs match exactly; the only differences are the error paths listed above.
- End to end through `ParserManager` with `--reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --tool-parser minimax_m3` (`parse_delta` per token and `parse`): reasoning, content, and tool calls match the bridge for `thinking_mode` enabled, unset, and disabled.
- `pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning`: the only failures are pre-existing on the base commit in this environment (gated Hugging Face models, a missing `cohere_melody`, an older local `xgrammar`).
- No GPU serving run: the change is confined to output parsing, and the differential and end-to-end checks above use the real tokenizer and chat template.

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_minimax_m3.py tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m3_tool_parser.py
```

## Details

- `vllm/parser/minimax_m3.py` is a tool-only engine config (like Granite); `<mm:think>` stays with `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser`. The terminals are the namespaced tags. `]<]minimax[>[` and `<tool_call>` are separate non-special added tokens in the checkpoint, so no marker is a single-token terminal, and M3 is excluded from the TOOL_END-token replay harness like PLaMo.
- The argument converter parses the `<invoke>` body with the Rust parser's element grammar: nesting limit 128, mixed text under `$text`, repeated tags collected into a list. It uses the tool schema to decide arrays versus objects, since list items are rendered as `<item>` children. Leaf values go through the existing `coerce_to_schema_type`. Empty elements become `[]` / `{}` under container schemas because the chat template renders empty lists and dicts that way. The schema is looked up from the tool slot whose raw arguments match, as `DeepSeekV4Parser` does.
- `stream_arg_deltas=False`: arguments are emitted once the `<invoke>` closes, as the Rust parser did; nested values are not prefix-stable while they are still being parsed.
- Text after `</tool_call>` is dropped, matching the Rust parser.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR moves `minimax_m3` off the bridge; vllm-project/vllm#51550 fixes the bridge's streaming flush and becomes moot once the bridge is removed.

commits.pr_title: [Profiler] Add per-session profiling controls to Python and Rust frontends
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Implement the Part D frontend/API split from #56542 on top of #57460.

`POST /start_profile` now accepts three optional per-session controls in both Python and Rust frontends:

- `profile_prefix`
- `delay_iterations`
- `max_iterations`

The same options are available through the Python `LLM` and `AsyncLLM` APIs. Worker profiler wrappers remain reusable across sessions while each session can select its own output name and iteration bounds.

For reviewer, main behavioral/logic changes are in
- `wrapper.py`: per-session overrides, output names, serialized start/stop
- `async_llm.py` / `llm_engine.py`: session guard, validation, engine-then-frontend start ordering
- `api_router.py`: typed request parsing and backwards compatible dispatch
- `executor/abstract.py`: override kwargs forwarded only when supplied, checked against the worker's `profile` signature before dispatch
- `gpu_worker.py`: final prefix validation + applying overrides
- `routes/profile.rs`, `engine-core-client/src/client.rs`: Rust request parsing and session guard

## Reviewed behavior and compatibility

- Unknown request fields are ignored, and an empty body (with or without `Content-Type: application/json`) starts a session with default settings.
- `vllm bench serve --profile` now sends an empty JSON request to `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` instead of the full inference payload, which also fixes profiling with the multipart `openai-audio` backend.
- A second start before an explicit stop returns HTTP 409 instead of silently discarding the new options. Notably this is different from previous behavior (allows duplicate start, 2nd start is ignored if profiler is running). I think once we introduce per-session overrides, this convention makes more sense.
- With `--api-server-count > 1`, session state cannot be coordinated across API processes, so the 409 guard is disabled (previous duplicate-start behavior is kept) and the frontend CPU profiler is disabled.
- Start/stop are serialized: an `asyncio.Lock` in `AsyncLLM`, a mutex in the Rust `EngineCoreClient`, and a lock around `WorkerProfiler.start()/stop()`. A start issued while a stop is in flight waits for it.
- `AsyncLLM` starts the frontend CPU profiler only after the engine start succeeds, so a failed start never leaves a frontend trace running. A cancelled start keeps the session active (it may have reached the engine); call `/stop_profile` before starting again.
- Iteration bounds apply to worker profiling. The frontend CPU profiler runs until `/stop_profile`, which remains required after worker auto-stop.
- New worker RPC arguments are keyword-only and sent only when supplied, so plain starts still work with out-of-tree workers. If overrides are supplied and the worker's `profile` does not accept them, the request is rejected before dispatch instead of failing on every rank.
- Values are validated once per entry point (`AsyncLLM`, `LLMEngine`, Rust route) plus once in the worker. Invalid and wrongly typed values (e.g. `"5"`, which is not coerced) return 400 from both frontends.
- `ProfilerConfig.should_profile_frontend` centralizes frontend eligibility for Torch CPU activity.
- The summary table is renamed from `profiler_out_<rank>.txt` to `<trace name>.profiler_out.txt` (including the prefix), so later sessions don't overwrite earlier ones. Documented in `docs/contributing/profiling.md`.

## Duplicate-work assessment

- This is the followup (Part D, frontend + api server changes) of #56542 after #57460 merged.
- It supersedes the Python-only iteration-control work in #35340 by adding Rust parity, prefix validation, compatibility tests, and overlapping-session handling.
- It differs from #51974, which proposes arbitrary backend profiler kwargs; this PR exposes only the typed prefix and iteration controls requested in #55207 and supports both frontends.

## Test plan and results

unit tests
```bash
pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/test_profile_api_router.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_profiler.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine.py \
  -k profil -q
# 167 passed

cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -E "test(profile)"
# 10 passed
```

manual tests (run against both frontends on 1x GB200; the Python frontend uses the same command without `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`)

server
```
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --max-model-len 512 \
  --profiler-config '{
    "profiler": "torch",
    "torch_profiler_dir": "/tmp/vllm-profile-rust"
  }'
```

verify `vllm bench serve --profile` works
```
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --dataset-name random \
  --input-len 32 \
  --output-len 16 \
  --num-prompts 2 \
  --profile

# benchmark ran successfully (2/2 requests) and produced trace + summary
/tmp/vllm-profile-rust# ls
rank0.1790749265595310494.pt.trace.json.gz  rank0.profiler_out.txt

# Python frontend also writes the AsyncLLM CPU trace
/tmp/vllm-profile-python# ls
<hostname>_<pid>.async_llm.1790749462449094114.pt.trace.json.gz
<hostname>_<pid>.async_llm.profiler_out.txt
rank0.1790749462507989442.pt.trace.json.gz
rank0.profiler_out.txt
```

verify per-session overrides produce expected traces
```
run_session() {
  prefix=$1
  delay=$2
  max=$3

  curl -fsS -X POST http://localhost:8000/start_profile \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"profile_prefix\":\"$prefix\",
         \"delay_iterations\":$delay,
         \"max_iterations\":$max}"

  curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"$MODEL\",
         \"prompt\":\"Profile this request\",
         \"max_tokens\":16,
         \"ignore_eos\":true}" >/dev/null

  curl -fsS -X POST http://localhost:8000/stop_profile
}

run_session short 0 2
run_session long 2 5

# requests successful and generated 2 different traces + summary with the expected names
/tmp/vllm-profile-rust# ls
long_rank0.1790749271762440330.pt.trace.json.gz   long_rank0.profiler_out.txt
short_rank0.1790749270550569175.pt.trace.json.gz  short_rank0.profiler_out.txt

/tmp/vllm-profile-python# ls
long_<hostname>_<pid>.async_llm.1790749470478729674.pt.trace.json.gz
long_<hostname>_<pid>.async_llm.profiler_out.txt
long_rank0.1790749469570197938.pt.trace.json.gz
long_rank0.profiler_out.txt
short_<hostname>_<pid>.async_llm.1790749469056878774.pt.trace.json.gz
short_<hostname>_<pid>.async_llm.profiler_out.txt
short_rank0.1790749467880203635.pt.trace.json.gz
short_rank0.profiler_out.txt
```

verify session guard and validation (same results on both frontends)
```
POST /start_profile                                  -> 200
POST /start_profile {"profile_prefix":"dup"}         -> 409
POST /stop_profile                                   -> 200
POST /start_profile {"profile_prefix":"../trace"}    -> 400
POST /start_profile {"max_iterations":-1}            -> 400
POST /start_profile {"delay_iterations":"5"}         -> 400
POST /start_profile (empty body, JSON content type)  -> 200
POST /stop_profile                                   -> 200
```

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Cursor) was used to help implement and test this change. I reviewed the changed code and will validate the behavior before marking the PR ready.

commits.pr_title: [Model][DeepSeek-V4.1] Permute mega-attention wq_b / wo_a while loading
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1's FlashMLA mega attention (the SM100 default) permutes `wq_b` rows and `wo_a` columns into the kernel's layout as a post-load step. That step is only correct when it runs before the linear quant hooks. This PR does the permutation in the weight loaders instead, so it no longer depends on post-load order. It is a prerequisite for #57733.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSv4.1 dummy-load startup crash on SM100 (DP4: `IndexError: index 1280 ...`; TP4: a size-mismatch `RuntimeError`).
- Fixes `reload_weights` (layerwise reload) for mega attention. On `main` the reloaded `wq_b` / `wo_a` are written in checkpoint order and `_fused_layouts_ready` skips the permutation, so accuracy collapses. Layerwise reload replays the loaders recorded at model init, so with this PR the reloaded shards are permuted again.
- Real loads are unchanged: after a TP4 cold load, checksums of every parameter and buffer (1605 per rank, after the quant hooks) match `main` on all 4 ranks.
- Removes `finalize_loaded_weights`, `_fused_layouts_ready`, `finalize_mega_attn_weights` and DSpark's `_finalize_attn` (+62 / −94).

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, real weights, `vllm serve`, GB200, mega attention (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, confirmed in the logs). GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. MegaMoE unless noted.

| config | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DP4 / EP4, mega attention | 0.892 | 0.896 |
| TP4 / EP4, mega attention | 0.910 | 0.911 |
| TP4 / EP4, default MoE backend: GSM8K, `reload_weights`, GSM8K | 0.897 → **0.000** | 0.906 → **0.898** |
| DP4 / EP4 + DSpark k=5: GSM8K, draft acceptance | 0.892, 51% | 0.896, 51% |
| DP4 / EP4, `--load-format dummy` | startup crash: `IndexError: index 1280 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 1280` | starts, serves a completion |
| TP4 / EP4, `--load-format dummy` | startup crash: `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (327680) must match the size of tensor b (1280)` | starts, serves a completion |

With MegaMoE, `reload_weights` collapses on both arms for a separate reason: the model-level post-load step (MegaMoE and mHC state) is not rerun after the layerwise reload finishes. #57733 reruns it; with #57733 and this PR, the same TP4 MegaMoE reload measures 0.901 → 0.898, while #57733 without this PR measures 0.900 → 0.002. The DP4 reload is not measurable on any arm: layerwise reload re-materializes the CPU-offloaded Engram table on the GPU and runs out of memory (pre-existing).

`tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py`: 2 passed. It loads `wq_b` / `wo_a` and their MXFP8 scales through the permuting loader and checks the permuted GEMMs against a reference that permutes the activation instead.

`pre-commit` passes.

Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this commit, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

## Details

**Root cause.** `permute_wq_b_` derives `head_dim` from `weight.shape[0]`. After the CuteDSL linear hook, `wq_b` is transposed to `[K, N]`, so `head_dim` is wrong and `q_fused_permutation` indexes out of bounds. The `wo_a` BMM hook likewise reshapes `wo_a` to 3D and packs its scales. A real load calls the permutation from inside `load_weights`, before the hooks, so it works there. A dummy load never calls `load_weights`. The model-level `process_weights_after_loading` then runs after the hooks and crashes.

**Fix.** `permute_on_load(param, perm, dim)` wraps the parameter's `weight_loader` with `composed_weight_loader`, so each loaded shard is gathered into the fused layout right after it is written. The wrapping happens in `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention.__init__`, for `wq_b.weight`, `wq_b.weight_scale`, `wo_a.weight` and `wo_a.weight_scale`. Each of these tensors is loaded by a single `weight_loader` call (no stacked mapping), so the whole local shard is present when the permutation runs. The quant hooks then see already-permuted tensors, exactly as `main`'s real load does.

The permutations are computed from the module's own `n_local_heads` / `head_dim` instead of tensor shapes. `n_local_heads // n_local_groups == WV_GROUP_SIZE` is already enforced in `__init__`.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for `mega attention wq_b`, `DeepSeek-V4.1 dummy load`, `fused_layout permute`, `finalize_loaded_weights` and `V4.1 mega attn`. #57977 touches `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` for MXFP8 activations but does not change the weight permutation.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Run decoder replay layers in CUDA graphs and trim in PIECEWISE graphs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Run the decoder-side SWA bounded replay layers (#58132) in CUDA graphs of their own, and trim them in PIECEWISE graph steps too. #58132 trims layers 21-39 to each prefill's last 128 tokens only on eager steps (above the model graph's capture range) and runs them eagerly there; those steps are often launch-bound (#58132 measured ~175 ms of kernel launches with the GPU waiting on a single 4K-8K prefill), and with a large `max_cudagraph_capture_size` nothing trims at all.

- `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager` (`nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py`), a `CudaGraphManager` owned by `DeepseekV41ModelState`, captures breakable PIECEWISE graphs of the replay layers, keyed by the replay batch's padded token count and reading the layer inputs from static buffers. Attention runs in their eager breaks: the replay batch mixes prefill tails and decodes, and the SWA and sparse MLA builders support uniform batches only.
- PIECEWISE model graphs of at least `compilation_config.decoder_replay_trim_threshold` padded tokens (768 by default) break out to the replay layers, which run on a replay batch (trimmed, or whole when nothing trims) and write their outputs to fixed buffers the graph's next segment reads. FULL graphs and smaller PIECEWISE ones keep the layers on the whole batch, as before.
- `_prepare_replay_batch` pads the replay batch to the smallest graph that fits the largest DP rank's replay batch and sets it on `DecoderReplayLayers` as one `ReplayBatch` (rows, forward context, graph runner). A replay batch above `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, possible only in eager steps, stays eager.
- Captures run the runtime path on a dummy batch, so the graphs read the buffers a real step's replay batch fills; on MRV2 the SWA KV insert stays inside the graph and reads the slot mapping by address.
- `ModelState.capture_inner_cudagraphs` is a new hook the runner calls after the model's capture; it is a no-op by default.
- On by default with breakable piecewise graphs (the default for DeepSeek-V4.1); `compilation_config.cudagraph_decoder_replay=false` turns it off. Also off under LoRA, prompt embeddings or on a non-first PP rank. Off keeps #58132's behavior.

No open PR runs the replay layers in graphs. #56752 (closed) captured them nested inside the model graph's capture; this captures them on their own and has the model graph break out to them.

## Benchmark

Prefill-only TTFT of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 at `f21ea3c947` (the last commit only adds the switch and renames), default CUDA graph settings, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix caching off, `max_tokens=1`. With the default capture range every 1K-128K prefill step is eager, so this measures the eager path, not PIECEWISE trimming. Median of 3 runs in ms; c1 is one request at a time, c8 is 8 concurrent. Off is `--no-swa-bounded-replay`; parent is df8fd42116 (main with #58132) with bounded replay on. Each topology ran all three on one node.

TP4 (repeats within ±2%; this PR's 1K c1 runs were 102/103/131 ms):

| ISL | conc | Off | Parent | This PR | vs off | vs parent |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K | c1 | 160.9 | 165.9 | **103.3** | 1.56x | **1.61x** |
| 1K | c8 | 324.3 | 333.7 | **269.1** | 1.21x | **1.24x** |
| 4K | c1 | 165.4 | 172.5 | **107.0** | 1.55x | **1.61x** |
| 4K | c8 | 505.3 | 505.2 | **442.7** | 1.14x | **1.14x** |
| 8K | c1 | 170.0 | 177.8 | **112.5** | 1.51x | **1.58x** |
| 8K | c8 | 963.5 | 683.9 | **562.9** | 1.71x | **1.21x** |
| 32K | c1 | 540.1 | 376.0 | **327.8** | 1.65x | **1.15x** |
| 32K | c8 | 3984.8 | 2714.7 | **2292.4** | 1.74x | **1.18x** |

commits.pr_title: [Attention][Model] FP8 KV cache for Triton DiffKV and MiMo-V2.6-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On main, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is silently ignored for MiMo-V2.6-Flash: its decoder and MTP layers build `Attention` without `cache_config`, so the KV cache stays BF16. Forwarding `cache_config` alone would turn this into a startup error on GPUs without FA3/FA4, where MiMo runs `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV`, which rejects quantized KV. This PR fixes both:

- `TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV` accepts `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` with per-tensor K/V scales and FP8 queries on CUDA. K and Q scales fold into the softmax scale; V scaling is applied once before writing the output or split-KV partials. Query quantization uses the existing Attention quantizer.
- The MiMo decoder and MTP layers (`mimo_v2.py`, `mimo_v2_mtp.py`) forward `cache_config`. Decoder layers clear `sliding_window` on the shared cache config, since MiMo's model-wide `sliding_window` (128) would otherwise be applied to its global layers.

On FA3/FA4 GPUs, the forwarding also enables FP8 through `FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV` (untested here).

No other open PR covers DiffKV FP8 or the MiMo KV cache dtype; #54341 (fp8_e5m2 in triton_attn) doesn't touch either.

Merge order with #58177: its `BLOCK_M=32` prefill path doesn't help with FP8 KV (0.96–1.01x, measured before the FP8-Q update), so whichever lands second adds `k.dtype == torch.bfloat16` to that gate.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py
```

FP8 is a new `kv_cache_dtype` parameter of the existing reference test, compared against the PyTorch reference on the dequantized cache. K/V scales are 0.3/0.7 to exercise rounding. Three focused FP8-Q cases cover prefill, 2D decode and split-KV decode, with a non-unit Q scale and the existing tolerance.

Initial serving validation, before the review follow-up, on DGX Spark (GB10), vLLM main 70fc359d: MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL, TP2 across two nodes, DFlash (k=3), 1 and 2 concurrent requests, same 17 GiB KV pool: this PR with `fp8` vs main (BF16); 128K runs compare this PR with `auto` vs `fp8`. The doubled KV cache size shows the MiMo forwarding takes effect; 128K needle retrieval shows global layers keep full attention.

## Test Result

Kernel tests on GB10: 99 passed (96 FP8 KV + 3 FP8 Q), 96 skipped (BF16 cases need FA3/FA4; they run in the H100 CI job). Real tiny target, MTP and DFlash constructors passed for BF16 and FP8. Pre-commit and the Python 3.10/3.12 mypy checks passed.

### Original BF16 versus FP8 comparison

These measurements precede the scale-hoisting and FP8-Q changes.

| | BF16 | FP8 |
|---|---|---|
| KV cache size (tokens) | 1,365,757 | 2,731,530 |
| GSM8K (300 questions, 5-shot) | 0.933 | 0.943 |
| Needle retrieval 16K / 32K / 128K | 8/8, 8/8, 4/4 | 8/8, 8/8, 4/4 |

In those original runs, FP8 TTFT was 4–7% higher at 16–32K prompts and ~15% higher at 128K; decode throughput shows no significant change. With `auto`, KV cache size is unchanged from main.

### Review follow-up

Compared the original PR FP8 implementation with this update on 2× DGX Spark, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL, TP2, DFlash k=3, 2048 batched tokens and the same 17 GiB KV pool. Both arms used the same pinned main-70fc359d production runtime and other patches; only the reviewed source differed. DFlash stayed on FlashInfer with BF16 Q and FP8 KV.

| | Original PR FP8 | Updated FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 16K TTFT, median | 7.397 s | 6.899 s (−6.7%) |
| 32K TTFT, median | 17.593 s | 15.548 s (−11.6%) |
| GSM8K, 300 questions | 281/300 | 279/300 |
| Needle retrieval 16K / 32K / 128K | 8/8, 8/8, 2/2 | 8/8, 8/8, 2/2 |

TTFT uses one warmup and three measured requests per length, c=1, 16 output tokens. All six paired prompt lengths matched, with 0.0% reported prefix-cache hits. This compares two FP8 implementations, not FP8 against BF16.

GSM8K uses the same first 300 questions, output was within margin of error

AI-assisted (OpenAI Codex, Claude). All changes reviewed by me.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Mistral pre-v11: don't fail requests on unexpected tool call JSON
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59222.

With a pre-v11 Mistral tokenizer (`--tool-call-parser mistral` on e.g. `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`), non-streaming tool call extraction in `MistralParser._legacy_extract_tool_calls` assumed the JSON after `[TOOL_CALLS]` is a list of `{"name", "arguments"}` objects. Any other valid JSON raised out of the parser, and nothing on the serving path catches it, so the whole request failed with a 400 or 500. That includes a bare object, a call without a name, a scalar or list of scalars, and a second `[TOOL_CALLS]` marker (which raised `ValueError` by design and put the entire model output in the error message). String `arguments` were also JSON-encoded a second time. Streaming did not raise but dropped bare objects and string arguments.

| model output | before |
| --- | --- |
| `[TOOL_CALLS][{"name":"get_weather","arguments":{}}][TOOL_CALLS]` | `ValueError` |
| `[TOOL_CALLS]{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {}}` | `TypeError` |
| `[TOOL_CALLS][1, 2, 3]`, `[TOOL_CALLS]["get_weather"]`, `[TOOL_CALLS]42`, `[TOOL_CALLS]"hello"` | `TypeError` |
| `[TOOL_CALLS][{"arguments": {}}]` | `KeyError` |
| `[TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "f", "arguments": "{\"a\": 1}"}]` | arguments returned as `"\"{\\\"a\\\": 1}\""` |

Both paths now decode the same way:

- a bare object is a single call
- a missing or non-string name becomes `""`, as in the v11+ path
- string `arguments` are kept as-is instead of being re-encoded
- output after a second `[TOOL_CALLS]` is trailing text, as in streaming; the first call is kept
- valid JSON that holds no call object is returned as content, like the existing invalid-JSON fallback

Streaming gets the same rules, so a bare object and string arguments produce the same calls as non-streaming.

Originally found by fuzzing every registered tool parser with fragments of its own marker tokens plus JSON junk; `mistral` was the only parser that raised. The current code change was pushed by a maintainer from #59308 so that this earlier PR carries the complete fix (the first version here only returned the unexpected shapes as content and left streaming and the double-encoding alone). #59226 is the other open PR for #59222.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py -v
```

New cases cover each shape in non-streaming and streaming and check both give the same calls. 16 of the 19 new cases fail on `main`.

Live A/B on 1x H200 was run on #59308 with this same diff: the same server and 14 chat completion requests at temperature 0 (each non-streaming and streaming, with `get_weather` and `add` tools; `tool_choice` auto single and parallel, required, named, none, a no-tool question, and a system prompt asking for a single call object with string arguments) ran against the branch and its merge base, and the normalized responses were diffed.

```bash
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser mistral --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35
```

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py -q
160 passed
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
commits.pr_body:
## Overview With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step. The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path. ## Claims - Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`. - No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint. ## Validation Setup: RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on 2 H200 GPUs, served with default settings plus MTP: ``` vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` Reproducer (script below): send a long prompt while another long prompt is still being processed, then send the exact same prompt again. The second request reuses the cached start of the prompt. - Before the fix, the second answer was garbage in 3 of 3 trials, for example `File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 # File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 ...`, while the first answer was a normal list of function names. - With the fix, both answers were normal in 3 of 3 trials. Other checks: - A single long prompt sent twice, with nothing else running, also came back broken in 4 of 7 runs at about 25k tokens before the fix, and in 0 of 12 runs after. - In an 8-agent coding-agent run (10 turns, full history resent each turn), 2 agents switched to word salad right after reusing their cached history and stayed broken. With the fix, and with MTP off, no agent broke. - New test `test_mamba_checkpoint_hash_maps_only_to_checkpoint_block` fails on main and passes with the fix. - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache` passes; the GPU part, `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`base` and `mtp`), was run on one H200.
repro.py ```python """Reproducer: with MTP on, sending the same long prompt twice can return garbage the second time. Server (any recent main): vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' Run: python repro.py http://localhost:8000/v1 Each trial sends a long prompt while another long prompt is running, then sends the same prompt again. The second answer reuses the cached start of the prompt. Before the fix it is often garbage; after the fix both answers are normal. """ import random import sys import threading from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="none") MODEL = client.models.list().data[0].id WORDS = "alpha beta gamma delta kernel buffer index cache shard block token commit".split() def long_prompt(seed, size): """Made-up Python code of about size characters, different for every seed.""" rng = random.Random(seed) lines = [] while sum(map(len, lines)) < size: lines.append(f"def {rng.choice(WORDS)}_{rng.choice(WORDS)}(x): return {rng.randrange(10**6)} " f"# {' '.join(rng.choices(WORDS, k=8))}\n") return "Here is a file:\n" + "".join(lines) + "\nList the first five function names, then summarize the file." def ask(prompt, max_tokens): out = client.chat.completions.create( model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "low"}}) # GLM-5.3: short thinking msg = out.choices[0].message thinking = getattr(msg, "reasoning", None) or getattr(msg, "reasoning_content", None) or "" return (thinking + (msg.content or "")).replace("\n", " ") def run_together(prompts, max_tokens): threads = [threading.Thread(target=ask, args=(p, max_tokens)) for p in prompts] for t in threads: t.start() for t in threads: t.join() # Whether a prompt is affected depends on its exact length; these lengths trigger it. for trial, size in enumerate([60000, 60000, 60000]): # Keep the server busy for a moment, as it would be in production. run_together([long_prompt(1000 + 10 * trial + k, 90000) for k in range(6)], 64) # A long request is running while the target prompt is processed for the first time. background = threading.Thread(target=ask, args=(long_prompt(10 * trial + 1, size), 300)) background.start() threading.Event().wait(0.3) target = long_prompt(10 * trial + 2, size) first = ask(target, 60) background.join() # The exact same request again. second = ask(target, 60) print(f"trial {trial}") print(f" first: {first[:100]}") print(f" second: {second[:100]}") ``` Example output on main (before the fix): ``` trial 0 first: **First five function names:** 1. `alpha_beta` 2. `index_token` 3. `buffer_cache` 4. `gamma_shard` 5 second: List the first five function names, then summarize the file. ## Details In align mode a request keeps its running state in the block after the last computed one, followed by `num_speculative_blocks` scratch blocks. A normal `allocate_new_blocks` call moves the old scratch blocks that fall below the new running state to the end of the table and nulls their slots. In a checkpoint step this was skipped (`if blocks_allocated and not checkpoint_block`). With MTP, the checkpoint position P is shifted one block down. When one of the previous step's scratch blocks sits at index `P // block_size - 1` (with k=1: the chunk starts one block below P), it occupies the natural slot of P. The checkpoint itself is written into a new block at `cdiv(end, block_size) - 2`, one index above it. In the same step, `cache_full_blocks` registers the unwritten scratch block under hash(P), and `_cache_partial_tail_block` then adds the real checkpoint block under the same hash. `get_one_block` returns the first block registered, so later hits at P resume from the scratch page. The entry stays until eviction, so every request that shares this prefix is affected. It happens when a prompt's final prefill chunk starts one block below the shifted checkpoint, so it depends on prompt length and on how much of each step's token budget other requests use. Overlapping long prompts make it much more likely. For example, with a second request of 22350 tokens, a first request of up to 23424 tokens triggers it (3/3) and one of 23440 tokens does not (0/3). The fix relocates scratch blocks below the checkpoint index (`block_idx < num_skipped_blocks - checkpoint_block`). A scratch block exactly at the checkpoint index stays and becomes the checkpoint block, since the worker exports the checkpoint into that column. Because relocated blocks are reused, checkpoint steps for already-allocated requests no longer need `num_speculative_blocks` extra new blocks. The allocation cap in `allocate_new_blocks` and the admission estimate in `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` both drop that term, so they stay equal. The existing `test_mamba_checkpoint_admission_matches_allocation` and the new test both check this. On unfixed builds, disabling MTP or prefix caching avoids the bug. Possible CI follow-up: no current job would catch this. The only nightly on this path, the B200 Kimi-K3 spec-decode GSM8K job, uses ~640-token prompts, and GSM8K accuracy does not move noticeably. A small extra phase in that job could catch this class of bug. After the GSM8K pass, it would send about 15 long prompts with lengths spread over one chunk-budget period, then send each again and check that the cached answer starts the same as a fresh computation. On GLM-5.3-Flash such a phase failed on unfixed main in 3 of 3 runs and passed with this fix in 3 of 3. I can send it as a separate PR if that is useful. AI assistance (Claude) was used; the change was reviewed and validated by the submitter. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Drop stale block hashes when a session truncates tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49377.

When a streaming-input session continues, `_update_request_as_session` truncates `_all_token_ids` at `num_computed_tokens`, discarding the last sampled (never-computed) output token. `update_block_hashes` only appends and the hasher resumes at `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size`, so if the discarded token completed a hash block, that hash kept identifying the replaced sequence and could later be committed under the stale identity — letting a request whose prefix matches the old tokens hit KV computed from the new ones. The fix drops the block hashes covering discarded tokens right where the token truncation happens; blocks fully inside the kept prefix stay valid.

## This PR carries #52806

This carries #52806 by @brianosaurus (original author unresponsive to review requests) with all review comments from @sawsa307 addressed:

- Removed the comment in `scheduler.py` that only described code behavior.
- Test no longer hardcodes the block size (`hash_block_size = scheduler.hash_block_size`).
- Test docstring shortened per AGENTS.md; details kept here instead.

The original author and contributors are credited via `Co-authored-by` trailers: Brian Woods (original #52806 author), Claude Opus 5 (original commit's co-author trailer), and Change72 (initial fix idea in #49377, requested by the reviewer). This is not a duplicate PR: #52806 has been stalled since the review round; this PR applies the identical fix with the requested changes so it can move forward, with full credit preserved.

Note on forward interaction with #58778: if #58778 (keep_end fold) lands first, this drop's lower bound should switch from `num_computed_tokens` to `keep_end`; conversely if this lands first, #58778 should keep the drop at `keep_end`.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=/tmp /Users/davidcheung/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -q -p skip_cleanup_plugin

uv tool run ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen4Exp FP8 PLE pinned lookup kernel failing to compile below SM89
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59868. On GPUs below SM89 (the report uses 4 × RTX 3090), Qwen4Exp with an FP8 E4M3FN PLE table and `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'` crashes in `profile_run`. The crash is a Triton `CompilationError` from `_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel`. This PR makes that kernel copy rows as raw bytes, so the FP8 type never enters its signature.

## Claims

- `_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel` now compiles and runs on sm_86 with an FP8 E4M3FN table, and it copies FP8 rows bit-exactly.
- On an A40, three existing FP8 pinned-lookup tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py` failed before this change. They now pass.
- BF16 lookups are unchanged: same bits, same speed.
- The module still imports when Triton is not installed.

## Validation

Hardware: a machine with 4 × NVIDIA A40 (sm_86). The reproducer uses one GPU. Software: vLLM commit `92044241a` (`0.30.1rc1.dev648+g92044241a`), with and without this PR, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12.12.

**Reproducer.** The reported path needs a checkpoint with FP8 PLE weights and a global scale. The public `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint has BF16 PLE weights and no scale. So the reproducer launches the kernel directly with a small FP8 tensor. Below is the core of the script that ran. The full script only adds prints and a `try`/`except`.

```python
import torch
from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.ngram_embedding import (
    _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel,
)

N, D, BLOCK_D = 4, 16, 16
device = torch.device("cuda", 0)
weight = torch.zeros(N, D, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=device)
ids = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
output = torch.zeros(1, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)

_lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel[(ids.numel(),)](
    weight, ids, output, D, 0, N, BLOCK_D=BLOCK_D,
)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

Run it from outside the source tree: `python -P repro_59868.py`.

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 3 of 3 failed | `CompilationError`, exit code 1 | | After | 2 of 2 passed | launch completes, exit code 0 |

Two of the "before" runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` image, and one used a source install. The "after" runs used the final patch. Three more runs on earlier versions of the patch also passed. Before the fix, every run showed the same error as the report:

```
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0:
def _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel(
^
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

The reproducer writes from an FP8 weight into a BF16 output. vLLM never does this, because `_lookup` requires `output.dtype == weight.dtype`. After the fix, that call copies the raw FP8 bytes. So the reproducer only shows that the launch compiles. The tests below check the values on the real path.

**Existing tests.**

```
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q --noconftest -k "pinned or uva"
```

`--noconftest` was used only because `tblib` was not installed locally.

- Before: `3 failed, 13 passed, 59 deselected`. All three fail with the error above: `test_ple_pinned_embedding_loads_on_cpu_and_looks_up_through_uva[True]`, `test_amd_pinned_embedding_output_written_under_compile[fp8]` and `test_amd_pinned_embedding_output_written_under_cudagraph_capture[fp8]`. They go through `_lookup` and check exact values.
- After: `16 passed, 59 deselected`. The full `test_ple.py` together with `tests/test_triton_utils.py` gives `88 passed`.

**Other checks.** These used one-off scripts that are not part of this PR.

- NVIDIA serving flow with FP8 on the A40 (`start_prefetch` → `forward` → `dequantize`): bit-exact against `weight[ids]` for row widths 3 and 160. With an ETP size of 2, rows owned by the other rank come out as zero bytes, in FP8 and in BF16.
- Large BF16 lookup with 160-element rows, compared row by row with `weight[ids]`: 7,000,000 and 8,388,608 rows gave 0 wrong rows, with byte offsets up to 2,684,354,240. Without the int64 row index (see Details), 7,000,000 rows hit `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.
- BF16 speed against the old kernel, reading a pinned host table through UVA: time ratio ×0.993 to ×1.03 for row widths 64 to 1024 and for 160 (the real model's width). Outputs were bit-identical.
- Import with Triton hidden (`sys.modules["triton"] = None`) passes. Without the placeholder change it fails with `AttributeError: module 'triton.language' has no attribute 'pointer_type'`.
- `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passes.

**CI gap.** On NVIDIA, CI does not run the GPU tests in `test_ple.py`, and no CI runner is below SM89. So CI cannot catch this bug if it comes back. The runs above are the validation. The AMD MI355 job does run `test_ple.py`, so it covers the new byte copy on AMD.

## Details

**Root cause.** The kernel's pointer parameters had no annotations, so Triton took their types from the tensors. An FP8 E4M3FN table became a `*fp8e4nv` parameter. Triton 3.7.1 accepts `fp8e4nv` only on compute capability 8.9 and higher. It rejects the type while it lowers the signature, before it compiles the body. That is why the error points at `1:0`, the `def` line. On the A40, a kernel with an empty body and one `float8_e4m3fn` pointer fails the same way. With `float8_e5m2` it compiles.

**Fix.** The kernel does no math on the values. Its only caller, `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding._lookup`, requires the output dtype to match the weight dtype. FP8 scaling happens later, in PyTorch (`dequantize`). So the kernel is a pure row gather. Both pointers are now annotated `tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8)`. The caller passes `row_bytes = embedding_dim * weight.element_size()` and sets `BLOCK_D = next_power_of_2(row_bytes)`. This works for FP8 and for BF16. `_reduce_etp_embeddings` in the same file already moves FP8 rows as raw bytes. The fix has to be in the signature, because the signature is where the error happens. A `uint8` pointer cast inside the body would come too late. A `.view(torch.uint8)` at the call site would fix `_lookup`, but not a direct launch with an FP8 tensor like the reproducer.

The fix also needs two more changes:

- `row_id` is now int64. Offsets are now in bytes, so for BF16 `row_id * row_bytes` is twice the old element offset. An int32 product would overflow at half as many rows as before. With `embedding_across_dp`, it would overflow at DP × `max_num_batched_tokens` ≥ 419,431 instead of 838,861 (for example, DP8 × 65,536). `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` is the usual vLLM idiom.
- `TritonLanguagePlaceholder` gets `uint8` and `pointer_type`. Python evaluates parameter annotations at import time, so without these names the module fails to import when Triton is missing. This is the first `tl.pointer_type` annotation in `vllm/`. mypy rejects it, so both lines carry `# type: ignore[valid-type]`.

**Limitations.**

- No end-to-end `vllm serve` run with an FP8 PLE checkpoint (see Reproducer). Only sm_86 was tested, not sm_80.
- `_engram_lookup_kernel` in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` also takes an FP8 E4M3FN table with no annotation, so it may fail the same way below SM89. It was not run. It does math on the values, so this byte-copy fix does not carry over, and it is not part of this PR.
- No model evaluation was run. The lookups are bit-exact in the tests above.

## E2E results (patch)

`vllm serve` with `-tp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 32768 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'`. The patch is applied on top of `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`. GSM8K is 5-shot, chat mode, thinking disabled (stderr ≈ ±0.7).

| Model | GPU | PLE dtype | Result | GSM8K flexible / strict | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | A100 (SM80) | FP8 E4M3, pinned host | starts and serves | 92.95 / 91.96 | 
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` | B200 (SM100) | FP8 E4M3, pinned host | bit-identical to unpatched | 92.49 / 91.51 |
| `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | B200 (SM100) | BF16, pinned host | bit-identical to unpatched | 93.40 / 92.34 |

"Bit-identical" means greedy decoding at batch size 1: 10/10 prompts and 640/640 tokens match the unpatched build, with exactly equal logprobs.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing while Prefill is still alive with the same engine ID**. Without recovery, vLLM's cached `_remote_agents` entry and prepared dlists can keep subsequent requests on the stale path.

A receive failure schedules a descriptor-free `check_remote_metadata(agent)` check. This queries **local metadata existence, not peer health**. Only confirmed absence makes the peer eligible for recovery; a transfer error or probe exception alone does not.

## Implementation

- Track failed and locally invalid peers in `NixlBaseConnectorWorker`. One `_cleanup_remote_engines()` pass handles both replacement and invalidation, reusing `_cleanup_remote_engine()` to release resources.
- Defer probes and cleanup while background handshakes are pending. For invalid peers, reject new reads and wait for all existing receive handles to settle before cleanup. Replacement cleanup retains its existing queued-request guard.
- Clear recovery state in the shared per-engine cleanup, including TTL eviction and shutdown. A peer that is both replaced and invalidated is cleaned once; the replacement's address mapping is preserved.
- Route new and handshake-ready requests through the pull worker's existing read entry point. After cleanup, a fresh request re-handshakes the unchanged engine ID and uses newly prepared descriptors. Failed requests are **not replayed with old remote block IDs**.

The production changes are in `nixl/base_worker.py` and `nixl/pull_worker.py`. Recovery remains **pull-only**, with an explicit push-mode TODO. There is no new router API, configuration, or metadata probe on successful transfers.

Following Yannik's review, tests reuse `TestPeerReplacement` and `FakeNixlWrapper` instead of a separate hand-built recovery fixture. The existing receive/HMA fixtures and push test stub initialize the new fields. Nick Hill's read/handshake simplification is retained with authorship preserved.

## Related Work and Scope

Related to #49238. This is a follow-up to merged #50047, not another replacement detector:

| Change | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| #50047 | A new engine ID is confirmed at the same address. |
| This PR | The engine ID is unchanged, but NIXL has lost the decoder's local peer metadata. |

Both now use one base-worker cleanup pass, rather than separate replacement and recovery passes. The scope split was discussed in [#50047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50047#issuecomment-5629552908).

#52232 addresses HMA failure propagation and is **not included here**. Recovering future requests does not by itself guarantee that the failed HMA request returns an error instead of invalid output. TTL policy and the native UCX race discussed in NIXL #1987 are also outside this patch's scope.

Stuck reads or handshakes defer recovery; this patch does not forcibly release active resources. Native cleanup exceptions propagate rather than being swallowed. Recovery is not a claim that every UCX failure is recoverable.

## Validation

### Refactor and CI

| Check | Result and revision scope |
| --- | --- |
| Local source-AST/mock regressions after the refactor and September 29 main merge | 32 passed: 20 previous recovery cases plus 12 existing receive-lifecycle cases. These external harnesses are not full-import vLLM tests. |
| Old-fixture negative control | The same 12 receive-lifecycle cases fail with the original missing-field fixtures. |
| Recorded-main behavioral negative control | 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passing controls. |
| Local pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` | Passed on the September 29 merged revision. |
| [Buildkite #91865](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91865), September 29 merged revision | NVIDIA KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**; AMD KV Connector shards **4/4 passed**. The overall build reports "passed and blocked"; not every defined pipeline job was executed. |
| [Subsequent automatic main merge](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8aba1056b6b811b4770fd6bba860b54835c84ca6), September 30 | Pre-commit and DCO passed. No full Buildkite result is attached to this new head at the time of this update; #91865 tested the preceding revision. |

The failures in earlier CI #91736 were missing recovery fields in fixtures that bypass the worker constructor. Those fixtures are now initialized, and the subsequent KV Connector shards pass.

Regression coverage includes confirmed-missing versus healthy/probe-error cases, same-ID re-handshake with fresh descriptors, pending-handshake gating, sibling-handle drain ordering, new-read rejection, healthy-peer isolation, replacement/invalidation overlap, notify-only requests, expiry accounting, cleanup exceptions, TTL eviction, and shutdown.

Local full-import pytest collection was blocked by missing `tblib` and the incomplete vLLM runtime environment; the 32 local cases are not a substitute for CI. There is **no new native NIXL/GPU or model-serving evaluation of the refactored revision**. Historical experiments below remain evidence only for their stated revisions and configurations.

### Reproduction Commands

From a vLLM checkout with the repository's test dependencies installed:

```bash
# Focused replacement and local-invalidation coverage.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -k TestPeerReplacement -v --tb=short

# Broader connector CPU regression suite.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  -m cpu_test -v --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/pull_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

These commands select the current tests; they are not presented as the exact Buildkite shard commands. The old `-k peer_recovery` selector no longer describes the consolidated tests.

<details>
<summary>Historical native and serving evidence, before the current refactor</summary>

### September 23 H20 validation

Full vLLM Python imports in isolated H20 containers: **357 selected CPU tests passed**, including 18 recovery cases; the corresponding main-only selection passed 339. Eight selected baseline cases produced 3 expected recovery assertion failures and 5 passes.

Real NIXL/UCX probes passed with 1 MiB CPU and GPU buffers. With the peer still alive, the probe deliberately removed local metadata, observed the stale-read failure, invoked patched cleanup, and explicitly reloaded the same agent's metadata for a byte-checked read. Healthy-peer reads continued working. Automatic re-handshake was covered separately by pytest.

Runtime: NIXL 1.4.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3. The rebased Python source used native extensions from the existing vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9` image, not a fresh CUDA build of main. No weights were loaded for this validation. This is not a model-serving, natural-disconnect, or NVLink/RDMA validation of the current revision.

[Exact commands, full selected logs, and native probe](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/34c74ce35e1f68958e5881a1907bf84d).

### Original TP1 P/D serving experiment

The original implementation was tested with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, NIXL 1.3.2, fp8 HMA KV, eager mode, `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`, and the existing TP1 packed-layout fix. With no active reads, a controlled hook removed only Decode's local remote metadata, retaining the Python cache. A real stale read failed with `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`; fresh requests automatically re-handshook the unchanged Prefill engine ID and returned the expected short answers.

The **recovery-only failed request still emitted 32 invalid tokens**. Adding #52232 and an API terminal-error follow-up produced a passing 10-request scenario: two normal controls, four controlled failures across Chat/Completion and streaming/non-streaming, and four fresh Chat recoveries. The failed requests emitted no generated content. This combined result must not be attributed to the recovery-only diff. Attribution for the HMA change belongs to Tyler Michael Smith.

The original recovery-only CPU selections passed 353 distinct cases across two runs. The combined recovery/HMA/API experiment passed 425 selected tests, not 425 tests of this standalone patch. Full original logs retain earlier failures and an independently wrong pre-injection arithmetic control.

This is controlled failure-path evidence, not general accuracy, natural transport-failure reproduction, multi-rank native-race coverage, or a guarantee of production readiness.

[Selected raw logs, response bodies/SSE, commands and patches](https://gist.github.com/xijiaat/a975858a507d6c45fd394b3675cc0ab9). Internal addresses and paths are anonymized. The HMA/API evidence is also reported in [#52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232#issuecomment-5552174526).

### Maintainer simplification

Nick Hill's [simplification](https://github.com/njhill/vllm/commit/7dc2a0eb49dbc62fdfc329885e663a672160cdec) was incorporated with authorship and sign-off preserved. It reuses main's in-flight-transfer guard rather than a second request-to-engine map: receive metadata remains available until the handles settle. The subsequent refactor retains that approach and moves cleanup into the base worker as suggested by Yannik Hinteregger.

</details>

## AI Assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and this report. The human submitter reviewed and approved the original contribution; subsequent compatibility adaptations remain subject to human review. Historical results and limited failure-path tests are not claims of comprehensive model evaluation or production readiness.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Malformed `$defs` in a tool schema should be a 400, not a 500
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

A tool schema containing `"$defs": null` turns a caller mistake into a 500.

`tools[].function.parameters` is an arbitrary caller-supplied dict, so `$defs` is whatever the request said it was. `_get_tool_schema_defs` read it as:

```python
defs = params.pop("$defs", {})
for def_name, def_schema in defs.items():
```

The `{}` default only covers the key being **absent**. An explicit `"$defs": null` — or a list, or a string — reaches `.items()` and raises `AttributeError`.

Nothing catches it on the way out:

`ToolParser.adjust_request` → `OnlineRenderer.render_chat` → `ChatCompletionServing.render_chat_request` → `create_chat_completion`

so the client gets a 500 for a request it simply got wrong.

```console
$ curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -d '{
    "model": "...", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],
    "tool_choice": "required",
    "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather",
      "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"string"}},"$defs":null}}}]
  }'
# AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'items'  ->  500
```

`_get_tool_schema_defs` is shared, so this reaches roughly 35 of the registered tool parsers. I found it by fuzzing `adjust_request` with malformed tool schemas across every parser in the registry; every one of them that got that far failed on the same input.

The boundary is narrow, and I checked the neighbours rather than assuming:

| `parameters` | `tool_choice="auto"` | `"none"` | `"required"` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{"$defs": null}` | ok | ok | **AttributeError** |
| `{"$defs": []}` | ok | ok | **AttributeError** |
| `{"$defs": "x"}` | ok | ok | **AttributeError** |
| `{"properties": null}` | ok | ok | ok |
| `{"required": null}` | ok | ok | ok |
| `parameters: null` | ok | ok | ok |

Only `$defs`, and only on the path that actually builds the JSON schema. A named `tool_choice` takes a different branch and is unaffected.

## The fix

Reject a non-object `$defs` with `VLLMValidationError`, which
`create_error_response` maps to a 400 naming `tools` as the offending parameter.

The duplicate-definition check right below it raised a plain `ValueError`:

```python
raise ValueError(
    f"Tool definition '{def_name}' has multiple schemas, which is not supported."
)
```

That is also caller-caused — two tools declaring the same `$defs` name with different schemas — and it also became a 500, so it moves to the same exception. I checked that nothing catches `ValueError` from this call, so the type change is not load-bearing anywhere.

### Overlap I checked

Three open PRs touch this function, and none of them fixes this:

- **#46170** (Avoid mutating tool parameters in `_get_tool_schema_defs`) replaces the `pop` with a non-mutating form but keeps `params.get("$defs", {})`, so the crash survives it verbatim. Last updated July 5, `mergeable_state=blocked`.
- **#50933** (Resolve `$ref`/`$defs` in tool schemas) adds ref resolution downstream and does not type-check `$defs`.
- **#49602** is scoped to the Cohere reasoning parser.

This change is one `isinstance` guard plus an exception type, so it should rebase cleanly onto whichever of those lands.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -v
```

`TestMalformedToolSchemaDefs` added to the file that already tests
`get_json_schema_from_tools`:

- `test_non_object_defs_is_a_client_error` — parametrized over `null`, `[]`, `"nope"`, `1`; asserts `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter == "tools"` and a message naming the tool
- `test_duplicate_def_names_is_a_client_error` — the `ValueError` → `VLLMValidationError` move
- `test_well_formed_defs_still_hoisted` — a real `$defs` is still hoisted to the top-level schema
- `test_absent_defs_still_works` — the common case, no `$defs` at all

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -q
170 passed, 15 warnings in 58.94s

$ pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -q
344 passed, 16 warnings in 120.42s
```

Reverting only `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` and running the new class:

```
$ pytest tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py -q -k MalformedToolSchemaDefs
FAILED ...::test_non_object_defs_is_a_client_error[null]
FAILED ...::test_non_object_defs_is_a_client_error[list]
FAILED ...::test_non_object_defs_is_a_client_error[string]
FAILED ...::test_non_object_defs_is_a_client_error[int]
FAILED ...::test_duplicate_def_names_is_a_client_error
5 failed, 2 passed, 163 deselected
```

The two that pass before and after are `well_formed_defs_still_hoisted` and
`absent_defs_still_works`, which is what makes them worth having.

Re-running the schema fuzz after the change, across every parser in the registry and two seeds, `adjust_request` no longer raises anything that is not a `VLLMClientError`.

```
$ ruff check <touched files>            # All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check <touched files>   # 2 files already formatted
```

The repo's local pre-commit hooks pass on the touched files (`check_spdx_header`, `check_init_lazy_imports`, `check_forbidden_imports`, `check_torch_cuda`, `check_boolean_context_manager`).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Disable AITER attention query quantization on RDNA3
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
RDNA3 has no low precision(fp8, fp4) WMMA support, so matmul input needs to be implicitly casted back to fp16/bf16. Within attention, they are (QxK) and (PxV). However, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` always enable Query quantization: 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1c3ef2ad4cabfbc2e5d74494b0b2bf8c3cb3f936/vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py#L187

That means quantizing Q on gfx11 causes several problems:
1. pure precision loss. The compute must still been done at f16 precision.
2. adds quantization overhead, calling F16 Q-> FP8.
3. As of now creating HUGE regression in Triton kernel(https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5601).
   Using TRITON=`3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.1.0a20260811`, the compiler has an uneven cost upcasting FP8 to BF16/FP16, and the Triton compiler **by default** cast matmul operands to FP16 instead of BF16, if they were both FP8.

   Reading assembly shows that casting to fp16 adds significant compute overhead(more cmp instructions), compared to explicit casting to bf16. For Gemma4 prefill attention kernel, it results in ~4x regression.

   ### Gemma4 full_attention Prefill kernel(16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim 512, causal), block_size 64, gfx1151
    
    | seq | TILE | fp8 Q (ms) | bf16 Q (ms) | bf16 faster | ratio |
    |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | 4096 | 16 | 385.487 | 80.455 | 79.1 % | **4.79×** |
    | 4096 | 32 | 360.010 | 85.832 | 76.2 % | **4.19×** |
    | 4096 | 64 | 655.943 | 131.885 | 79.9 % | **4.97×** |
    | 16384 | 16 | 6129.764 | 1370.336 | 77.6 % | **4.47×** |
    | 16384 | 32 | 5643.135 | 1403.945 | 75.1 % | **4.02×** |
    | 16384 | 64 | 10439.351 | 2213.269 | 78.8 % | **4.72×** |
    | 32768 | 16 | 24553.301 | 5692.050 | 76.8 % | **4.31×** |

    Leaving Q in bf16 bypasses this compiler behavior. We are investigating into this issue inside Triton compiler but adding this change in vLLM is quicker and also solves problem 1 and 2.

*** 

## Test Result
Gemma4 32768-in / 32-out, `--max-num-seqs 1`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--num-prompts 4`, gfx1151.

| backend | KV | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| TRITON_ATTN | bf16 | 146005.21 | 73.58 |
| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | bf16 | 20117.60 | 50.59 |
| TRITON_ATTN | fp8 | 164764.79 | 85.09 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Size per-region replicate flags by each region's block count
commits.pr_body:
## Background

With P_TP > D_TP (e.g. PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode), each decoder rank reads a block from several prefill ranks. Each local descriptor gets a replicate flag: full-attention regions are **SPLIT** (each rank fills its head slice), MLA regions are **REPLICATE** (whole block read once).

`_fa_desc_replicated` assumed every region holds the same number of blocks. HiSparse breaks this: host-resident MLA regions hold `hisparse_host_num_blocks`, GPU regions hold `num_blocks`. Every P_TP > D_TP handshake into a HiSparse decoder failed with `AssertionError: FA desc flags N != num_fa_descs M`.

## Fix

Build the flags the same way `_build_fa_local` builds the descriptors: same region order, `region_num_blocks[i] * block_size_ratio` per region. Companion fix for the same topology: #60108. No other open PR touches this function.

## Validation

**main vs. this PR**, checked against the descriptors `_build_fa_local` emits:

| Region layout | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Equal block counts | OK | OK |
| HiSparse, unequal block counts | assert | OK |
| Unequal counts that divide evenly | flags silently wrong | OK |
| Layer-name routing, region listed twice | flags silently wrong | OK |

**Unit:** `test_tp_mapping.py` + `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`: 121 passed.

**E2E** (GLM-5.3, 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 HiSparse decode, with #60108): main asserts on the first request. With both fixes, 8 one-hour agentic benchmark points ran with 0 errors and a 100% decoder prefix-cache hit rate. That run used an earlier revision of this fix that produces identical flags for this topology.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Return NumPy descriptors from mixed-memory local registration
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With mixed DRAM/VRAM registration (HiSparse host-resident regions), `register_local_xfer_handler` returned the local descriptors as a list of tuples instead of its annotated `np.ndarray`. The P_TP > D_TP split path (`_build_local_splits_from_plan`) calls `.tolist()` on them, so a PCP8/DCP8 prefiller feeding a HiSparse decoder failed the NIXL handshake with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist'`. Companion fix for the same topology: #60107.

**Fix:** keep the Nx3 `uint64` array in the mixed-memory path. DRAM rows get device 0 via `blocks_data[desc_is_dram, 2] = 0`, and the DRAM/VRAM subsets are array slices.

## Validation

**Unit:** `test_mixed_memory_local_descriptors_split_by_memory_type` now asserts the returned descriptors are an `np.ndarray` (fails before the fix). `test_tp_mapping.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`: 498 passed (3 GPU e2e tests left to CI).

**End to end**, GLM-5.3 on 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8/EP8 prefill → DP8/EP8 HiSparse decode, MTP3:

| vLLM | Result |
|---|---|
| main + #60107 | decoder fails in `_build_local_splits_from_plan` on the first request; no KV transferred |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] One-pass dequantize and a gather-sized grid for the compressed K cache
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton` walks a V4.1 prefill's whole compressed prefix once per layer, and it did so on a fixed `(num_reqs, 128)` grid with a per-token loop that issued twenty-two memory operations. Two changes here: the grid follows the length being gathered, and a token is dequantized in one pass. They compose — the first raises how many dependent-load chains are in flight, the second cuts the work each chain does.

## Sizing the grid

Each worker walks its slice of the sequence one token at a time, and every step is a dependent load: block table entry, then the page it points at, then the token inside it. The loop is bound by that chain's latency rather than by bandwidth, so the grid has to hold enough chains in flight to cover it. At batch size 1 the whole grid was 128 workgroups on a 256-CU gfx950, while a V4.1 prefill gathers the entire compressed prefix once per layer: about 3.1k serial steps per worker at a 399k-token context.

A caller that knows a host-side bound on `gather_len` now passes it and the grid follows, aiming for eight steps per worker. The DeepSeek-V4.1 ROCm compressed-KV gather takes that bound from `prefill_seq_lens_cpu`, which the metadata already carries, so nothing new syncs with the device. Callers that pass no bound keep the previous width, so the CUDA paths are unchanged. The same file's sliding-window gather keeps the old width on purpose: it reads at most `window_size` plus the chunk's query tokens.

## Dequantizing in one pass

The per-token loop walked the 448 fp8 bytes in seven 64-byte quantization blocks, loading a scale byte per block and storing per block, then copied the 64 bf16 tail in four chunks of sixteen. The seven blocks tile 448 exactly, so the `qblock_start < fp8_dim` branch and the `offsets < fp8_dim` masks never excluded anything; what they cost is twenty-two memory operations per token where four will do.

The MXFP8 record added for the FlashMLA V4.1 layout already reads its token in one load, scales it with a reshape, and stores it once. This gives the `fp8_ds_mla` kernel the same shape. `scale_dim * quant_block` is 512 against an fp8 region of 448, so the tail of the tile reads into the token's own bf16 bytes, is scaled by a scale nothing reads, and is dropped by the store mask; the token record is 576 bytes, so the read stays inside it, and a `tl.static_assert` holds that.

## Kernel time

MI355X, one request, `torch.profiler` over ten calls after five warm-ups, same inputs on every arm:

| context | main | grid by length | + one-pass dequantize | vs main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | 95.9 us | 18.9 us | **6.6 us** | **14.5x** |
| 32,768 | 480.1 us | 61.2 us | **19.9 us** | **24.1x** |
| 131,072 | 1945.6 us | 230.2 us | **65.9 us** | **29.5x** |
| 399,360 | 7767.2 us | 914.5 us | **343.9 us** | **22.6x** |
| 1,048,576 | 20359.1 us | 2385.1 us | **912.0 us** | **22.3x** |

The grid's own gain settles at −88% from 32k up, because `gather_num_workers` caps at 8192 and a 1M gather wants more; the one-pass dequantize then takes a further 62–71% at every length, since it changes the work per token rather than the parallelism. The combined factor peaks at 131k and eases to 22x beyond it: past the cap the grid stops widening, so the longest contexts keep the per-token win but not the rest of the parallelism one.

A width of 8192 is where widening stops paying. Sweeping the grid by hand on a 1M-token gather, with the dequantize already in one pass, 2048 and 8192 workers are within 3% of each other and 65536 buys 2.5%; at 131k a width of 65536 is 12% *slower* than 2048. The cap is not what bounds the long-context number.

## Correctness

The second commit adds a kernel rather than editing one: ROCm gets `_dequantize_and_gather_k_one_pass_kernel`, CUDA keeps `_dequantize_and_gather_k_kernel`. Neither had a test — the existing cases import the deepseek_v4 copy, and the two V4.1 cases cover the 528 B MXFP8 and 288 B NVFP4 records, both SM100-only. The 584 B record these two kernels decode is the only one a ROCm V4.1 server gathers.

The third commit covers both kernels, parametrized on the ROCm dispatch so each runs wherever the test lands. It checks that grid width cannot move the output — `num_workers` is only the per-token loop stride and each iteration writes its own row, so four widths must be byte-equal — and that the rows match a host-side UE8M0 dequantization, which is what catches a wrong tile or scale.

## End-to-end

MI355X, TP 4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM at `af1c01499` (this branch's parent, so the arms differ only in this PR's two files), [official MI355X recipe][recipe] config minus its `--speculative-config`. Two things the recipe omits are needed to boot: `--ulimit memlock=-1` on the container (the engram table pins 23.6 GiB per rank) and #57036 in every arm, without which the AITER fused-expert path indexes the expert weights with the -1 cudagraph padding sentinel and all ranks fault during the startup profile run.

`vllm bench serve --random-output-len 8` so the number is prefill, 40 prompts per repetition at concurrency 4. A repetition replays the previous one's prompts, so the first is cold and the rest hit the prefix cache. Warm rows are the mean of eight repetitions ± their standard deviation; the whole table was measured twice with identical seeds and agrees to within 2 %.

| shape | main | grid by length | + one-pass dequantize | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 131k, warm cache | 354.7 ± 4.3 ms | 224.8 ± 1.4 ms | **201.6 ± 1.8 ms** | **−43.2 %** |
| 131k, cold | 15638.0 ± 2.9 ms | 14409.9 ± 30.5 ms | 13985.4 ± 11.2 ms | **−10.6 %** |
| 32k, warm cache | 158.7 ± 9.4 ms | 137.2 ± 11.0 ms | **129.1 ± 9.9 ms** | **−18.7 %** |
| 32k, cold | 2223.7 ± 109.9 ms | 2192.5 ± 121.9 ms | 2096.3 ± 108.4 ms | −5.7 % |

The changes compose at 131k: the grid takes 36.6 %, the one-pass dequantize a further 10.3 %. The 32k cold row is four fresh-server runs per arm and every arm's spread is ~5 %, so it should not be read as a gain — a microbenchmark puts the gather at ~1 % of a cold 32k prefill, against 11 % of a warm one.

Percentiles over the 320 pooled warm requests per cell (`--save-detailed`); a single repetition puts only four requests above p90 and swings by 25 %:

| shape | | main | grid by length | + one-pass dequantize |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 131k | p50 | 389.6 ms | 250.0 ms | **219.8 ms** |
| | p90 | 402.7 ms | 259.7 ms | **232.7 ms** |
| | p99 | 549.1 ms | 335.8 ms | **313.5 ms** |
| 32k | p50 | 180.8 ms | 146.3 ms | **140.2 ms** |
| | p90 | 188.8 ms | **200.7 ms** | **165.6 ms** |
| | p99 | 201.6 ms | 216.8 ms | **195.8 ms** |

GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, `tests/evals/gsm8k`) with tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py : 0.9022 on the merge base against 0.9045 with the branch. Both runs report a zero invalid rate.

GSM8K via InferenceX's lm-eval config (`infx/evals/gsm8k.yaml`, 5-shot, chat template, strict and flexible extraction): 0.9765 / 0.9757 on the unmodified nightly image against 0.9742 / 0.9735 with this PR's two files applied 
Both arms carry the #57036 padding-sentinel fix, without which the server does not start on MI355X.


## Notes

The grid width becomes data-dependent. This call site is prefill-only, and `num_workers` is read inside the kernel through `tl.num_programs(1)`, so any width is correct — a replayed capture would use the width it recorded and only lose the speedup. #56686 goes the other way for the candidate-block kernels, which do run inside decode captures.

The sliding-window gather in the same file keeps the old width: 40 calls totalling 0.49 ms in the profile above. `deepseek_v4` carries a copy of this kernel with the same fixed 128 and is left alone; that path deserves its own numbers.

#42504 attacks this kernel from a different angle — gather only the top-k slots the sparse attention reads, instead of dequantizing the whole prefix and discarding most of it. That is the larger win and this does not conflict with it: after this change the gather is still 32.4 ms of a 97.8 ms prefill kernel budget.
